Charged the card, replayed the Stripe webhook, and the invoice flipped to **Paid** with the photos still shown. Both `79cdea90` and `a6b89e3c` are confirmed fixed in the running app (not just in tests) and are marked resolved.

### Journey 2: A day in the life of a cleaner

**Pass.** `/field` listed 7 jobs today in correct ascending start-time order (9:00 ×5, 13:00, 17:00), all belonging to qa-cleaner only. Opened the 17:00 job (an existing seeded job with a real 3-item checklist), which showed the full get-in-the-door brief (address, entry method, parking, pet notes) on the day list. Clocked in — elapsed time ticked live from 0h 0m. Checked off all 3 checklist tasks (Kitchen/Wipe countertops, Bathroom/Scrub tub, Living Room/Vacuum carpet) and attached an after-photo to one task; confirmed the office side (`/quality/:job_id`) shows the checklist as Done with the stored photo path. Filed an unsafe-condition incident report with no photo (photo correctly not required — only required for damage/missing-item types) and confirmed it appears on the office's `/quality` index as a notification-feed item, attributed to qa-cleaner with a timestamp. Clocked out and finished the job (status → completed); per-job earnings and the pay-period running total displayed correctly.

Isolation checks all correct: opening another cleaner's job by URL redirected to `/field` with "This job is not assigned to you."; `/schedule` and `/timesheets` both redirected to `/field` with "You don't have access to that page."

### Journey 3: Schedule chaos — reminders, changes, acknowledgment, audit

**Pass.** Confirmed a reminder token via `GET /reminders/confirm/:token` → "Confirmed" page; the `/schedule` board then showed "Confirmed" next to that job. Rescheduled a different job's start time using the board's inline time-picker (the control that actually notifies — see Issues for the other "Edit" affordance that doesn't) → board showed "Unacknowledged Push - Job moved from X to Y." As the cleaner, saw a loud orange "Schedule change" banner on `/field` with an Acknowledge button; after acknowledging, the owner's board showed "Acknowledged Push - ...". Cancelled a job on the board — it stayed visible with a "Cancelled" label and "Unacknowledged Push - Cancelled." Backdated that notification's `pushed_at` more than 10 minutes via psql (sanctioned time manipulation) — on next board read the status correctly flipped to "Escalated SMS - Cancelled" (escalation is computed on-read per the code, not a periodic job). `/audit` filtered by Changed-by + Record type=Job showed the reschedule ("Start time: 09:00:00 → 09:45:00") and both cancellations with correct old→new values, reconstructing who changed what.

One defect found and filed (see Issues): the board's alternate "Edit Job" dialog silently skips the schedule-change notification that the inline time-picker sends for the same underlying change.

### Journey 4: Preferred cleaner continuity

**Pass.** Created a weekly recurring plan (4 visits) on the Journey 1 property with qa-cleaner set as preferred cleaner — all 4 materialized jobs defaulted to the preferred cleaner (verified in the DB and via each job's cleaner-select on the board). Reassigned the first visit to a different cleaner on the board and got the expected "This visit is now assigned away from the client's preferred cleaner" warning. Verified the plan's own `cleaner_id` and the three later visits were untouched — the one-off substitution did not rewrite the plan. Created a second weekly plan (3 visits, different property) with no preferred cleaner — visits materialized unassigned, and reassigning one produced no warning at all.

### Journey 5: Payroll close

**Pass.** The current pay period (2026-07-06 – 2026-07-12) already had a mix of hourly and piece-rate completed jobs for qa-cleaner. `/timesheets` showed per-job amounts that check out exactly: hourly jobs = rate × clocked hours (e.g. $25/hr × 2.495h = $62.37; $20/hr × ~11s ≈ $0.06), piece-rate jobs pay a flat amount regardless of duration or repeated clock-ins (one job had two time entries and still paid its $80.00 flat rate once, not twice) — running pay-period total $241.00 checked out as the exact sum of the six line items. Nulled one entry's `clocked_out_at` via psql (sanctioned) — the entry immediately showed "Missing clock-out" with an inline resolve form, the pay-period total dropped to exclude that entry's pay, and the Export CSV button became genuinely disabled (`disabled` attribute confirmed, not just styled) with a "Resolve the unresolved time entry before exporting" message. Resolved the clock-out via the timesheet form — pay recomputed ($240.61) and the export button re-enabled. Exported via the properly parameterized URL (`GET /timesheets/export?start_date=...&end_date=...`, matching what the "Export CSV" button itself generates) — the returned CSV row (`qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test,27.19,6,$240.61`) matches the on-screen total exactly.

One low-severity, not-user-reachable defect found and filed (see Issues): hitting `/timesheets/export` directly without the query params crashes instead of failing gracefully.

## Issues

- **[High, app]** `79cdea90-9fc5-4806-97f2-e844e177490c` — Checklist template "Add Task" never adds a row; templates can only ever be saved with 0 tasks through the UI (Journey 1).
- **[Medium, app]** `a6b89e3c-3035-477f-9e03-243e4439b59c` — Compounding bug found while diagnosing the above: the same button's `JS.dispatch` builds an unescaped CSS id selector that throws a SyntaxError whenever the template's id starts with a digit (~62% of UUIDs).

This is why the Evidence section below has no file paths to point to.

## Rescheduling a job via the "Edit Job" dialog doesn't push a schedule-change alert (only the inline time input does) (ID: ca2cb170-1d1b-41e7-b33a-4fc455f390e0)

**Severity:** medium | **Scope:** app | **Status:** resolved | **Story:** 843

Journey 3 QA (schedule chaos — reminders, changes, acknowledgment, audit), step "Reschedule a different job's start time from the board — verify the change is pushed as a schedule-change alert."

The board (/schedule) offers two different ways to change a job's start time:
1. The inline `<input type="time" data-test="job-{id}-start-time-input">` next to the date (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/index.ex:131-139), wired to `phx-change="reschedule_job:{id}"` → `handle_event("reschedule_job:" <> job_id, ...)` (index.ex:271-289), which calls `Scheduling.update_job/3` AND `notify_schedule_change/3`. Confirmed working: changing this input produced "Unacknowledged Push - Job moved from 10:30 AM to 11:15 AM" on the board.
2. The "Edit" button, which opens `JobFormComponent` in `:edit` mode (a full Date/Start Time/End Time/Price/Pay type form) — its `handle_event("save", ..., %{assigns: %{action: :edit}})` (job_form_component.ex:260) also calls `Scheduling.update_job/3` for the same fields, but the parent's `handle_info({JobFormComponent, {:job_updated, _job}}, socket)` (index.ex:297-299) only does `assign(:editing_job_id, nil) |> load_week()` — it never calls `notify_schedule_change`. Reproduced directly: edited a job's start time from 09:00 to 10:30 via "Edit" → Save Changes, then checked `notifications` table for that job_id — no new schedule_change row was created (only the pre-existing unrelated reminder notification).

Impact: a user who reschedules using the more prominent, full-featured "Edit Job" form (the same one used to change price/pay type) gets no cleaner notification at all — the change is silent. Only the narrow inline time-only quick-edit notifies. This contradicts the story's expectation that every schedule mutation reaches the affected cleaner loudly, and is inconsistent given both paths call the same `Scheduling.update_job/3` underneath.

Suggested fix: have the `{JobFormComponent, {:job_updated, job}}` handler in index.ex also call `notify_schedule_change/3` when start_time/end_time changed (mirroring the cancel_job and reassign_job handlers), or consolidate both time-edit affordances onto one code path.

**Resolution:** Rescheduling via the board's "Edit Job" dialog (JobFormComponent's :edit save path) now pushes the same cleaner-facing schedule-change notification the inline board controls already send. Extracted notify_schedule_change/3, format_time_12h/1, and notifications_ready?/2 out of ScheduleLive.Index into a new shared module, CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.ScheduleNotifier (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/schedule_notifier.ex), and updated Index to delegate to it. JobFormComponent's :edit handler now compares the job's scheduled_date/start_time/end_time before and after Scheduling.update_job/3, and calls ScheduleNotifier.notify_schedule_change/3 with a "Job moved from <date> <start>-<end> to <date> <start>-<end>" summary whenever any of those fields materially changed; a pay-rate/price-only save stays silent. cleaner_id is untouched by this dialog so no comparison was needed there. Added two regression tests to job_form_component_test.exs: one asserting a schedule_change notification is created (correct cleaner_id, :pending status, summary mentions old/new times) when the edit dialog reschedules, and one asserting no notification is created for a price-only edit. Verified: MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean; mix spex for 843/833/834 (19 tests, 0 failures); full mix test suite (163 tests, 0 failures); mix format --check-formatted clean. No dev server/compile touched.

The inline `<input type="time" data-test="job-{id}-start-time-input">` next to the date (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/index.ex:131-139), wired to `phx-change="reschedule_job:{id}"` → `handle_event("reschedule_job:" <> job_id, ...)` (index.ex:271-289), which calls `Scheduling.update_job/3` AND `notify_schedule_change/3`. Confirmed working: changing this input produced "Unacknowledged Push - Job moved from 10:30 AM to 11:15 AM" on the board.
2. The "Edit" button, which opens `JobFormComponent` in `:edit` mode (a full Date/Start Time/End Time/Price/Pay type form) — its `handle_event("save", ..., %{assigns: %{action: :edit}})` (job_form_component.ex:260) also calls `Scheduling.update_job/3` for the same fields, but the parent's `handle_info({JobFormComponent, {:job_updated, _job}}, socket)` (index.ex:297-299) only does `assign(:editing_job_id, nil) |> load_week()` — it never calls `notify_schedule_change`. Reproduced directly: edited a job's start time from 09:00 to 10:30 via "Edit" → Save Changes, then checked `notifications` table for that job_id — no new schedule_change row was created (only the pre-existing unrelated reminder notification).

Impact: a user who reschedules using the more prominent, full-featured "Edit Job" form (the same one used to change price/pay type) gets no cleaner notification at all — the change is silent. Only the narrow inline time-only quick-edit notifies. This contradicts the story's expectation that every schedule mutation reaches the affected cleaner loudly, and is inconsistent given both paths call the same `Scheduling.update_job/3` underneath.

Suggested fix: have the `{JobFormComponent, {:job_updated, job}}` handler in index.ex also call `notify_schedule_change/3` when start_time/end_time changed (mirroring the cancel_job and reassign_job handlers), or consolidate both time-edit affordances onto one code path.

**Resolution:** Rescheduling via the board's "Edit Job" dialog (JobFormComponent's :edit save path) now pushes the same cleaner-facing schedule-change notification the inline board controls already send. Extracted notify_schedule_change/3, format_time_12h/1, and notifications_ready?/2 out of ScheduleLive.Index into a new shared module, CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.ScheduleNotifier (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/schedule_notifier.ex), and updated Index to delegate to it. JobFormComponent's :edit handler now compares the job's scheduled_date/start_time/end_time before and after Scheduling.update_job/3, and calls ScheduleNotifier.notify_schedule_change/3 with a "Job moved from <date> <start>-<end> to <date> <start>-<end>" summary whenever any of those fields materially changed; a pay-rate/price-only save stays silent. cleaner_id is untouched by this dialog so no comparison was needed there. Added two regression tests to job_form_component_test.exs: one asserting a schedule_change notification is created (correct cleaner_id, :pending status, summary mentions old/new times) when the edit dialog reschedules, and one asserting no notification is created for a price-only edit. Verified: MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean; mix spex for 843/833/834 (19 tests, 0 failures); full mix test suite (163 tests, 0 failures); mix format --check-formatted clean. No dev server/compile touched.

## GET /timesheets/export crashes with raw Phoenix.ActionClauseError if start_date/end_date query params are missing (ID: 6fb028fa-8d88-4d88-b44f-4fa311ada02b)

**Severity:** low | **Scope:** app | **Status:** resolved | **Story:** 838

Journey 5 QA (payroll close), step "Export the CSV (GET /timesheets/export via authenticated_curl.sh)".

lib/cleaner_crm_web/controllers/timesheet_export_controller.ex:6 defines only `show(conn, %{"start_date" => start_date, "end_date" => end_date})` with no fallback clause. Hitting `GET /timesheets/export` without both query params (e.g. a bare curl, a bookmarked/typed URL, a stray monitoring probe) crashes with `Phoenix.ActionClauseError` (no function clause matching in show/2) instead of a clean 400/redirect — confirmed via `authenticated_curl.sh /timesheets/export -i` returning the full Phoenix debug error page (which in dev leaks the whole Plug.Conn, including session cookie value, user struct, etc. in the response body).

Not reachable through the normal UI: the "Export CSV" button on /timesheets (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/timesheet_live.ex:119-126) always redirects to the export URL with both params filled in from the current pay period, and is disabled entirely while any time entry is unresolved (confirmed correct — this is the expected "export is blocked" behavior from the story). This is a defensive-programming gap on the controller, not a user-facing functional bug: add a fallback clause that redirects to /timesheets or renders a friendly error when params are missing, rather than crashing.

**Resolution:** TimesheetExportController.show/2 now has a fallback clause: missing or malformed start_date/end_date params redirect to /timesheets with a "Choose a pay period to export" flash instead of raising (dates parsed with Date.from_iso8601, not the bang variant). Verified: 163/163 tests green.

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint do
  use Phoenix.Endpoint, otp_app: :cleaner_crm

  # The session will be stored in the cookie and signed,
  # this means its contents can be read but not tampered with.
  # Set :encryption_salt if you would also like to encrypt it.
  @session_options [
    store: :cookie,
    key: "_cleaner_crm_key",
    signing_salt: "IOeVZsWZ",
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  socket "/live", Phoenix.LiveView.Socket,
    websocket: [connect_info: [session: @session_options]],
    longpoll: [connect_info: [session: @session_options]]

  # Serve at "/" the static files from "priv/static" directory.
  #
  # When code reloading is disabled (e.g., in production),
  # the `gzip` option is enabled to serve compressed
  # static files generated by running `phx.digest`.
  plug Plug.Static,
    at: "/",
    from: :cleaner_crm,
    gzip: not code_reloading?,
    only: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths(),
    raise_on_missing_only: code_reloading?

  # Code reloading can be explicitly enabled under the
  # :code_reloader configuration of your endpoint.
  if code_reloading? do
    socket "/phoenix/live_reload/socket", Phoenix.LiveReloader.Socket
    plug Phoenix.LiveReloader
    plug Phoenix.CodeReloader
    plug Phoenix.Ecto.CheckRepoStatus, otp_app: :cleaner_crm
  end

  plug Phoenix.LiveDashboard.RequestLogger,
    param_key: "request_logger",
    cookie_key: "request_logger"

  plug Plug.RequestId
  plug Plug.Telemetry, event_prefix: [:phoenix, :endpoint]

  plug Plug.Parsers,
    parsers: [:urlencoded, :multipart, :json],
    pass: ["*/*"],
    json_decoder: Phoenix.json_library(),
    body_reader: {CleanerCrmWeb.CacheBodyReader, :read_body, []}

  plug Plug.MethodOverride
  plug Plug.Head
  plug Plug.Session, @session_options
  plug CleanerCrmWeb.Router
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Application do
  # See https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/Application.html

  @moduledoc false

  use Application

  @impl true
  def start(_type, _args) do
    children = [

      CleanerCrm.Repo,

      {Phoenix.PubSub, name: CleanerCrm.PubSub},

      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint
    ]

    # for other strategies and supported options
    opts = [strategy: :one_for_one, name: CleanerCrm.Supervisor]
    Supervisor.start_link(children, opts)
  end

  # Tell Phoenix to update the endpoint configuration
  # whenever the application is updated.
  @impl true
  def config_change(changed, _new, removed) do
    CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.config_change(changed, removed)
    :ok
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.DataCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the setup for tests requiring
  access to the application's data layer.

  You may define functions here to be used as helpers in
  your tests.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      alias CleanerCrm.Repo

      import Ecto
      import Ecto.Changeset
      import Ecto.Query
      import CleanerCrmTest.DataCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    :ok
  end

  @doc """
  Sets up the sandbox based on the test tags.
  """
  def setup_sandbox(tags) do
    pid = Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.start_owner!(CleanerCrm.Repo, shared: not tags[:async])
    on_exit(fn -> Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.stop_owner(pid) end)
  end

  @doc """
  A helper that transforms changeset errors into a map of messages.

      assert {:error, changeset} = Accounts.create_user(%{password: "short"})
      assert "password is too short" in errors_on(changeset).password
      assert %{password: ["password is too short"]} = errors_on(changeset)

  """
  def errors_on(changeset) do
    Ecto.Changeset.traverse_errors(changeset, fn {message, opts} ->
      Regex.replace(~r"%{(\w+)}", message, fn _, key ->
        opts |> Keyword.get(String.to_existing_atom(key), key) |> to_string()
      end)
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines test helpers for creating
  entities via the `CleanerCrm.Users` context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def unique_user_email, do: "user#{System.unique_integer()}@example.com"
  def valid_user_password, do: "hello world!"

  def valid_user_attributes(attrs \\ %{}) do
    Enum.into(attrs, %{
      email: unique_user_email()
    })
  end

  def unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, user} =
      attrs
      |> valid_user_attributes()
      |> Users.register_user()

    user
  end

  def user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs)

    token =
      extract_user_token(fn url ->
        Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, url)
      end)

    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

    user
  end

  def user_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    user_scope_fixture(user)
  end

  def user_scope_fixture(user) do
    Scope.for_user(user)
  end

  def set_password(user) do
    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: valid_user_password()})

    user
  end

  def extract_user_token(fun) do
    {:ok, captured_email} = fun.(&"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")

    # `fun` delivers through the real mailer (Swoosh's test adapter), so
    # this confirmation/login email it just sent is sitting in the
    # calling process's mailbox — an internal detail of building a
    # confirmed fixture user, not something the spec itself sent. Left
    # there, it's the *oldest* `{:email, _}` message, and
    # `assert_email_sent/1` always matches the oldest one first — so any
    # later, spec-relevant `assert_email_sent` would wrongly match this
    # one instead. Drain it now so it can't shadow that later assertion.
    receive do
      {:email, ^captured_email} -> :ok
    after
      0 -> :ok
    end

    [_, token | _] = String.split(captured_email.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
    token
  end

  def override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) when is_binary(token) do
    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(t in Users.UserToken,
        where: t.token == ^token
      ),
      set: [authenticated_at: authenticated_at]
    )
  end

  def generate_user_magic_link_token(user) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = Users.UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
    CleanerCrm.Repo.insert!(user_token)
    {encoded_token, user_token.token}
  end

  def offset_user_token(token, amount_to_add, unit) do
    dt = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(:second), amount_to_add, unit)

    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(ut in Users.UserToken, where: ut.token == ^token),
      set: [inserted_at: dt, authenticated_at: dt]
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, AccountsRepository, MembersRepository}
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{InvitationRepository, InvitationNotifier}
  alias CleanerCrm.Authorization
  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def subscribe_account(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account")
  end

  def subscribe_member(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member")
  end

  defp broadcast_account(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account", message)
  end

  defp broadcast_member(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member", message)
  end

  def list_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(scope.user.id)
  end

  def get_account(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case AccountsRepository.get_account(id) do
      nil ->
        nil

      account ->
        case Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account.id) do
          false -> nil
          true -> account
        end
    end
  end

  def get_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    account = AccountsRepository.get_account!(id)
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account.id)
    account
  end

  def create_account(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.create_account_with_owner(attrs, scope.user.id) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:created, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def update_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.update_account(account, attrs) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:updated, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def delete_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.delete_account(account) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:deleted, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def change_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)
    Account.changeset(account, attrs)
  end

  def list_account_members(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.list_account_members(account_id)
  end

  def add_user_to_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:created, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:deleted, member})
      {:ok, member}

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the test case to be used by
  tests that require setting up a connection.

  Such tests rely on `Phoenix.ConnTest` and also
  import other functionality to make it easier
  to build common data structures and query the data layer.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      # The default endpoint for testing
      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

      # Import conveniences for testing with connections
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.ConnTest
      import CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    {:ok, conn: Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()}
  end

  @doc """
  Setup helper that registers and logs in users.

      setup :register_and_log_in_user

  It stores an updated connection and a registered user in the
  test context.
  """
  def register_and_log_in_user(%{conn: conn} = context) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

    opts =
      context
      |> Map.take([:token_authenticated_at])
      |> Enum.into([])

    %{conn: log_in_user(conn, user, opts), user: user, scope: scope}
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given `user` into the `conn`.

  It returns an updated `conn`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, opts \\ []) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Users.generate_user_session_token(user)

    maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, opts[:token_authenticated_at])

    conn
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:user_token, token)
  end

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(_token, nil), do: nil

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) do
    CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at)
  end
end

import Config

# Only in tests, remove the complexity from the password hashing algorithm
config :bcrypt_elixir, :log_rounds, 1

# Configure your database
#
# The MIX_TEST_PARTITION environment variable can be used
# to provide built-in test partitioning in CI environment.
# Run `mix help test` for more information.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Repo,
  username: "postgres",
  password: "postgres",
  hostname: "localhost",
  database: "cleaner_crm_test#{System.get_env("MIX_TEST_PARTITION")}",
  pool: Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox,
  pool_size: System.schedulers_online() * 2

# We don't run a server during test. If one is required,
# you can enable the server option below.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  http: [ip: {127, 0, 0, 1}, port: 4002],
  secret_key_base: "pKeS+s2UVTkO2arvvgQLttUR3McIVtITSdLygq0I9T9C5M+7mGuWBFFVOWsO/ZMR",
  server: false

# In test we don't send emails
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Mailer, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test

# Never reach the real Stripe API in test — see CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Test
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
  adapter: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Test

# Oban runs inline in test — jobs execute synchronously in the calling
# process instead of a background queue, per the background-jobs-oban ADR.
config :cleaner_crm, Oban, testing: :inline

# Never reach the real Twilio API in test — see CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Test
config :cleaner_crm, :sms_delivery_adapter, CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Test

# Disable swoosh api client as it is only required for production adapters
config :swoosh, :api_client, false

# Print only warnings and errors during test
config :logger, level: :warning

# Initialize plugs at runtime for faster test compilation
config :phoenix, :plug_init_mode, :runtime

# Enable helpful, but potentially expensive runtime checks
config :phoenix_live_view,
  enable_expensive_runtime_checks: true

# Sort query params output of verified routes for robust url comparisons
config :phoenix,
  sort_verified_routes_query_params: true

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint do
  use Phoenix.Endpoint, otp_app: :cleaner_crm

  # The session will be stored in the cookie and signed,
  # this means its contents can be read but not tampered with.
  # Set :encryption_salt if you would also like to encrypt it.
  @session_options [
    store: :cookie,
    key: "_cleaner_crm_key",
    signing_salt: "IOeVZsWZ",
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  socket "/live", Phoenix.LiveView.Socket,
    websocket: [connect_info: [session: @session_options]],
    longpoll: [connect_info: [session: @session_options]]

  # Serve at "/" the static files from "priv/static" directory.
  #
  # When code reloading is disabled (e.g., in production),
  # the `gzip` option is enabled to serve compressed
  # static files generated by running `phx.digest`.
  plug Plug.Static,
    at: "/",
    from: :cleaner_crm,
    gzip: not code_reloading?,
    only: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths(),
    raise_on_missing_only: code_reloading?

  # Code reloading can be explicitly enabled under the
  # :code_reloader configuration of your endpoint.
  if code_reloading? do
    socket "/phoenix/live_reload/socket", Phoenix.LiveReloader.Socket
    plug Phoenix.LiveReloader
    plug Phoenix.CodeReloader
    plug Phoenix.Ecto.CheckRepoStatus, otp_app: :cleaner_crm
  end

  plug Phoenix.LiveDashboard.RequestLogger,
    param_key: "request_logger",
    cookie_key: "request_logger"

  plug Plug.RequestId
  plug Plug.Telemetry, event_prefix: [:phoenix, :endpoint]

  plug Plug.Parsers,
    parsers: [:urlencoded, :multipart, :json],
    pass: ["*/*"],
    json_decoder: Phoenix.json_library(),
    body_reader: {CleanerCrmWeb.CacheBodyReader, :read_body, []}

  plug Plug.MethodOverride
  plug Plug.Head
  plug Plug.Session, @session_options
  plug CleanerCrmWeb.Router
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint do
  use Phoenix.Endpoint, otp_app: :cleaner_crm

  # The session will be stored in the cookie and signed,
  # this means its contents can be read but not tampered with.
  # Set :encryption_salt if you would also like to encrypt it.
  @session_options [
    store: :cookie,
    key: "_cleaner_crm_key",
    signing_salt: "IOeVZsWZ",
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  socket "/live", Phoenix.LiveView.Socket,
    websocket: [connect_info: [session: @session_options]],
    longpoll: [connect_info: [session: @session_options]]

  # Serve at "/" the static files from "priv/static" directory.
  #
  # When code reloading is disabled (e.g., in production),
  # the `gzip` option is enabled to serve compressed
  # static files generated by running `phx.digest`.
  plug Plug.Static,
    at: "/",
    from: :cleaner_crm,
    gzip: not code_reloading?,
    only: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths(),
    raise_on_missing_only: code_reloading?

  # Code reloading can be explicitly enabled under the
  # :code_reloader configuration of your endpoint.
  if code_reloading? do
    socket "/phoenix/live_reload/socket", Phoenix.LiveReloader.Socket
    plug Phoenix.LiveReloader
    plug Phoenix.CodeReloader
    plug Phoenix.Ecto.CheckRepoStatus, otp_app: :cleaner_crm
  end

  plug Phoenix.LiveDashboard.RequestLogger,
    param_key: "request_logger",
    cookie_key: "request_logger"

  plug Plug.RequestId
  plug Plug.Telemetry, event_prefix: [:phoenix, :endpoint]

  plug Plug.Parsers,
    parsers: [:urlencoded, :multipart, :json],
    pass: ["*/*"],
    json_decoder: Phoenix.json_library(),
    body_reader: {CleanerCrmWeb.CacheBodyReader, :read_body, []}

  plug Plug.MethodOverride
  plug Plug.Head
  plug Plug.Session, @session_options
  plug CleanerCrmWeb.Router
end

      import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],

defmodule CleanerCrm.JourneyFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared prerequisite setup for `test/journeys/` feature tests: an
  owner and a cleaner, both with a known password, sharing one
  account — the minimum every journey needs before it can log in
  through the browser and drive the rest of the flow for real.
  """

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Returns `%{owner:, cleaner:, account:, owner_scope:, password:}`.

  `owner` and `cleaner` both have `password` set (from
  `valid_user_password/0`) so a Wallaby session can log in as either
  through the real `/users/log-in` form.
  """
  def account_with_owner_and_cleaner(attrs \\ %{}) do
    owner = user_fixture() |> set_password()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(
        owner_scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Journey QA Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    owner_scope = %{owner_scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}

    cleaner = user_fixture() |> set_password()
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id, :member)

    %{
      owner: owner,
      cleaner: cleaner,
      account: account,
      owner_scope: owner_scope,
      password: valid_user_password()
    }
  end

  @doc "Logs the given user into the Wallaby `session` via the real password form."
  def log_in(session, user, password) do
    import Wallaby.Query

    session
    |> Wallaby.Browser.visit("/users/log-in")
    |> Wallaby.Browser.fill_in(css("#login_form_password_email"), with: user.email)
    |> Wallaby.Browser.fill_in(css("#user_password"), with: password)
    |> Wallaby.Browser.click(button("Log in only this time"))
  end

  @doc "Clears cookies so the next `log_in/3` starts from a clean session."
  def log_out(session), do: Wallaby.Browser.Cookies.delete_cookies(session)
end

defmodule Wallaby.Feature do
  @moduledoc """
  Helpers for writing features.

  You can `use` or `import` this module.

  ## use Wallaby.Feature

  Calling this module with `use` will automatically call `use Wallaby.DSL`.

  When called with `use` and you are using Ecto, please configure your `otp_app`.

  ```
  config :wallaby, otp_app: :your_app
  ```
  """

  defmacro __using__(_) do
    quote do
      ExUnit.Case.register_attribute(__MODULE__, :sessions)

      use Wallaby.DSL
      import Wallaby.Feature

      setup context do
        if context[:test_type] == :feature do
          metadata = unquote(__MODULE__).Utils.maybe_checkout_repos(context[:async])

          start_session_opts =
            [metadata: metadata]
            |> unquote(__MODULE__).Utils.put_create_session_fn(context[:create_session_fn])

          get_in(context, [:registered, :sessions])
          |> unquote(__MODULE__).Utils.sessions_iterable()
          |> Enum.map(fn
            opts when is_list(opts) ->
              unquote(__MODULE__).Utils.start_session(opts, start_session_opts)

            i when is_number(i) ->
              unquote(__MODULE__).Utils.start_session([], start_session_opts)
          end)
          |> unquote(__MODULE__).Utils.build_setup_return()
        else
          :ok
        end
      end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Defines a feature with a message.

  Adding `import Wallaby.Feature` to your test module will import the `Wallaby.Feature.feature/3` macro. This is a drop in replacement for the `ExUnit.Case.test/3` macro that you normally use.

  Adding `use Wallaby.Feature` to your test module will act the same as `import Wallaby.Feature`, as well as configure your Ecto repos properly and pass a `Wallaby.Session` into the test context.

  ## Sessions

  When called with `use`, the `Wallaby.Feature.feature/3` macro will automatically start a single session using the currently configured capabilities and is passed to the feature via the `:session` key in the context.

  ```
  feature "test with a single session", %{session: session} do
    # ...
  end
  ```

  If you would like to start multiple sessions, assign the `@sessions` attribute to the number of sessions that the feature should start, and they will be pass to the feature via the `:sessions` key in the context.

  ```
  @sessions 2
  feature "test with a two sessions", %{sessions: [session_1, sessions_2]} do
    # ...
  end
  ```

  If you need to change the headless mode, binary path, or capabilities sent to the session for a specific feature, you can assign `@sessions` to a list of keyword lists of the options to be passed to `Wallaby.start_session/1`. This will start the number of sessions equal to the size of the list.

  ```
  @sessions [
    [headless: false, binary: "some_path", capabilities: %{}]

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistItemComponent do
  @moduledoc """
  A single checklist task: check it off, and attach before/after photo
  proof.

  Each task gets its own stateful component instance so its
  `:before_photo`/`:after_photo` uploads are scoped independently per
  task — a job's checklist can carry many tasks, each needing its own
  before/after slot, uploaded and consumed on its own.

  ## Offline-tolerant uploads

  A `CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo` row is created in `:pending` state the
  moment an upload starts — its first progress callback, before any
  bytes have landed in storage — and flipped to `:uploaded` only once
  the file finishes. If the connection drops (or this LiveView process
  itself restarts) before that flip, the pending row survives in the
  database: the next time this component mounts for that task, it
  finds the still-pending row (instead of creating a duplicate) and
  shows a "tap to retry" affordance that re-opens the same file picker.

  This is a manual retry, not true offline queuing — capturing a photo
  with no signal at all and having it upload itself once connectivity
  returns, with no action from the cleaner, would need client-side
  storage (e.g. a service worker or local queue) that a plain
  LiveView-uploads implementation doesn't have. That's out of scope
  here; a dropped upload waits, visibly, for the cleaner to tap retry.

  ## Assigns

  | Assign        | Type            | Required | Description                       |
  |---------------|-----------------|----------|------------------------------------|
  | id            | string          | yes      | LiveComponent DOM id                |
  | current_scope | `Scope.t()`     | yes      | caller scope, used for all context calls |
  | item          | `ChecklistItem.t()` | yes | the checklist item this instance renders |

  Notifies the parent LiveView with `send(self(), :checklist_changed)`
  after any change, so it can reload the checklist and pass fresh
  items back down.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Quality`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality

  @impl true
  def render(assigns) do
    ~H"""
    <li id={@id} class="py-2 border-b border-base-200 last:border-none">
      <div class="flex items-start gap-2">
        <button
          type="button"
          data-test={"checklist-item-#{@item.id}"}

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistItemComponent do
  @moduledoc """
  A single checklist task: check it off, and attach before/after photo
  proof.

  Each task gets its own stateful component instance so its
  `:before_photo`/`:after_photo` uploads are scoped independently per
  task — a job's checklist can carry many tasks, each needing its own
  before/after slot, uploaded and consumed on its own.

  ## Offline-tolerant uploads

  A `CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo` row is created in `:pending` state the
  moment an upload starts — its first progress callback, before any
  bytes have landed in storage — and flipped to `:uploaded` only once
  the file finishes. If the connection drops (or this LiveView process
  itself restarts) before that flip, the pending row survives in the
  database: the next time this component mounts for that task, it
  finds the still-pending row (instead of creating a duplicate) and
  shows a "tap to retry" affordance that re-opens the same file picker.

  This is a manual retry, not true offline queuing — capturing a photo
  with no signal at all and having it upload itself once connectivity
  returns, with no action from the cleaner, would need client-side
  storage (e.g. a service worker or local queue) that a plain
  LiveView-uploads implementation doesn't have. That's out of scope
  here; a dropped upload waits, visibly, for the cleaner to tap retry.

  ## Assigns

  | Assign        | Type            | Required | Description                       |
  |---------------|-----------------|----------|------------------------------------|
  | id            | string          | yes      | LiveComponent DOM id                |
  | current_scope | `Scope.t()`     | yes      | caller scope, used for all context calls |
  | item          | `ChecklistItem.t()` | yes | the checklist item this instance renders |

  Notifies the parent LiveView with `send(self(), :checklist_changed)`
  after any change, so it can reload the checklist and pass fresh
  items back down.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Quality`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality

  @impl true
  def render(assigns) do
    ~H"""
    <li id={@id} class="py-2 border-b border-base-200 last:border-none">
      <div class="flex items-start gap-2">
        <button
          type="button"
          data-test={"checklist-item-#{@item.id}"}
          phx-click="toggle"
          phx-target={@myself}
          class={["btn btn-sm btn-circle btn-outline shrink-0", @item.checked && "btn-success"]}

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.NewClientToPaidInvoiceTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 1 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): a cleaning business
  owner takes a client from first contact through a paid invoice —
  client -> property -> checklist template -> quote -> job -> the
  cleaner's checklist proof -> invoice -> payment. Two actors, so two
  browser sessions (see `@sessions 2` below) rather than juggling one
  session's cookies between owner and cleaner.

  Not async: the Stripe webhook step hits the endpoint directly with
  `Req` (not through the browser), which only shares the sandboxed
  transaction correctly under `{:shared, self()}` mode — enabled when
  `async: false` (see `Wallaby.Feature`'s setup).
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling

  @sessions 2

  feature "client to property to template to quote to job to invoice to paid", %{
    sessions: [owner_session, cleaner_session]
  } do
    %{owner: owner, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} = account_with_owner_and_cleaner()

    owner_session = log_in(owner_session, owner, password)

    # Client + property with full access details
    owner_session =
      owner_session
      |> visit("/clients/new")
      |> fill_in(css("#client_name"), with: "Journey1 QA Client")
      |> check(css("#client_card_on_file"))
      |> click(button("Save Client"))
      |> assert_has(css("h1", text: "Journey1 QA Client"))
      |> click(link("Add Property"))
      |> fill_in(css("#property_service_address"), with: "742 Evergreen Terrace")
      |> fill_in(css("#property_lockbox_code"), with: "4517")
      |> fill_in(css("#property_pet_notes"), with: "Friendly dog (Max)")
      |> click(button("Save Property"))
      |> assert_has(css("body", text: "742 Evergreen Terrace"))

    property_id =
      Wallaby.Browser.current_url(owner_session)
      |> String.split("/properties/")
      |> List.last()

    # Checklist template — the exact flow that was broken (Add Task
    # never added a row) and then fixed; this is its regression test.
    owner_session =
      owner_session
      |> visit("/quality/templates/new")
      |> fill_in(css("#template_name"), with: "Journey1 Standard Clean")
      |> Wallaby.Browser.execute_script(
        "document.querySelector('#template_property_id').value = arguments[0]; document.querySelector('#template_property_id').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));",
        [property_id]
      )
      |> click(css("[data-test='add-template-item-button'] input"))
      |> fill_in(css("input[placeholder='Kitchen']"), with: "Kitchen")
      |> fill_in(css("input[placeholder='Counters wiped down']"), with: "Wipe countertops")
      |> click(button("Save Template"))
      |> assert_has(css("table", text: "Journey1 Standard Clean"))

    # Per-room quote
    owner_session
    |> visit("/quotes/new")
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='quote[client_name]']"), with: "Journey1 QA Client")
    |> Wallaby.Browser.execute_script(
      "document.querySelector('select[name=\"quote[pricing_model]\"]').value = 'per_room'; document.querySelector('select[name=\"quote[pricing_model]\"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));",
      []
    )
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='quote[bedroom_count]']"), with: "2")
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='quote[bathroom_count]']"), with: "1")
    |> click(css("[data-test='send-quote-button']"))
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='quote-status']", text: "Sent"))

    # Job for today, assigned to the cleaner, hourly
    today = Date.utc_today() |> Date.to_iso8601()

    owner_session
    |> visit("/schedule/jobs/new")
    |> Wallaby.Browser.execute_script(
      """
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[property_id]"]').value = arguments[0];
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[property_id]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[date]"]').value = arguments[1];
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[date]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[start_time]"]').value = '09:00:00';
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[start_time]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[end_time]"]').value = '11:00:00';
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[end_time]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[pay_type]"]').value = 'hourly';
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[pay_type]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[cleaner_id]"]').value = arguments[2];
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[cleaner_id]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      """,
      [property_id, today, to_string(cleaner.id)]
    )
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='job[agreed_price]']"), with: "80")
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='job[hourly_rate]']"), with: "25")
    |> click(css("[data-test='save-job-button']"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "scheduled"))

    job = Scheduling.list_jobs(account_with_owner_and_cleaner_scope(owner)) |> hd()

    # Cleaner: open the job, clock in, complete the checklist with a
    # photo, clock out, finish
    cleaner_session
    |> log_in(cleaner, password)
    |> visit("/field/jobs/#{job.id}")
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-in-button']"))
    |> attach_file(css("input[name='after_photo']"),
      path: Path.expand("../support/fixtures/files/test_photo.png", __DIR__)
    )
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "photo attached"))
    |> click(css("[data-test^='checklist-item-']"))
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-out-button']"))
    |> click(css("[data-test='mark-complete-button']"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Complete"))

    # Owner: invoice shows proof of work, charge card, webhook -> Paid
    invoice = Billing.list_invoices(account_with_owner_and_cleaner_scope(owner)) |> hd()

    owner_session
    |> visit("/invoices/#{invoice.id}")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Proof of Work"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Wipe countertops"))
    |> click(button("Charge card on file"))

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.NewClientToPaidInvoiceTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 1 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): a cleaning business
  owner takes a client from first contact through a paid invoice —
  client -> property -> checklist template -> quote -> job -> the
  cleaner's checklist proof -> invoice -> payment. Two actors, so two
  browser sessions (see `@sessions 2` below) rather than juggling one
  session's cookies between owner and cleaner.

  Not async: the Stripe webhook step hits the endpoint directly with
  `Req` (not through the browser), which only shares the sandboxed
  transaction correctly under `{:shared, self()}` mode — enabled when
  `async: false` (see `Wallaby.Feature`'s setup).
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling

  @sessions 2

  feature "client to property to template to quote to job to invoice to paid", %{
    sessions: [owner_session, cleaner_session]
  } do
    %{owner: owner, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} = account_with_owner_and_cleaner()

    owner_session = log_in(owner_session, owner, password)

    # Client + property with full access details
    owner_session =
      owner_session
      |> visit("/clients/new")
      |> fill_in(css("#client_name"), with: "Journey1 QA Client")
      |> check(css("#client_card_on_file"))
      |> click(button("Save Client"))
      |> assert_has(css("h1", text: "Journey1 QA Client"))
      |> click(link("Add Property"))
      |> fill_in(css("#property_service_address"), with: "742 Evergreen Terrace")
      |> fill_in(css("#property_lockbox_code"), with: "4517")
      |> fill_in(css("#property_pet_notes"), with: "Friendly dog (Max)")
      |> click(button("Save Property"))
      |> assert_has(css("body", text: "742 Evergreen Terrace"))

    property_id =
      Wallaby.Browser.current_url(owner_session)
      |> String.split("/properties/")
      |> List.last()

    # Checklist template — the exact flow that was broken (Add Task
    # never added a row) and then fixed; this is its regression test.
    owner_session =
      owner_session
      |> visit("/quality/templates/new")
      |> fill_in(css("#template_name"), with: "Journey1 Standard Clean")
      |> Wallaby.Browser.execute_script(
        "document.querySelector('#template_property_id').value = arguments[0]; document.querySelector('#template_property_id').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));",
        [property_id]
      )
      |> click(css("[data-test='add-template-item-button'] input"))
      |> fill_in(css("input[placeholder='Kitchen']"), with: "Kitchen")
      |> fill_in(css("input[placeholder='Counters wiped down']"), with: "Wipe countertops")
      |> click(button("Save Template"))
      |> assert_has(css("table", text: "Journey1 Standard Clean"))

    # Per-room quote
    owner_session
    |> visit("/quotes/new")
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='quote[client_name]']"), with: "Journey1 QA Client")
    |> Wallaby.Browser.execute_script(
      "document.querySelector('select[name=\"quote[pricing_model]\"]').value = 'per_room'; document.querySelector('select[name=\"quote[pricing_model]\"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));",
      []
    )
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='quote[bedroom_count]']"), with: "2")
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='quote[bathroom_count]']"), with: "1")
    |> click(css("[data-test='send-quote-button']"))
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='quote-status']", text: "Sent"))

    # Job for today, assigned to the cleaner, hourly
    today = Date.utc_today() |> Date.to_iso8601()

    owner_session
    |> visit("/schedule/jobs/new")
    |> Wallaby.Browser.execute_script(
      """
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[property_id]"]').value = arguments[0];
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[property_id]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[date]"]').value = arguments[1];
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[date]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[start_time]"]').value = '09:00:00';
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[start_time]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[end_time]"]').value = '11:00:00';
      document.querySelector('input[name="job[end_time]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[pay_type]"]').value = 'hourly';
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[pay_type]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[cleaner_id]"]').value = arguments[2];
      document.querySelector('select[name="job[cleaner_id]"]').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      """,
      [property_id, today, to_string(cleaner.id)]
    )
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='job[agreed_price]']"), with: "80")
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='job[hourly_rate]']"), with: "25")
    |> click(css("[data-test='save-job-button']"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "scheduled"))

    job = Scheduling.list_jobs(account_with_owner_and_cleaner_scope(owner)) |> hd()

    # Cleaner: open the job, clock in, complete the checklist with a
    # photo, clock out, finish
    cleaner_session
    |> log_in(cleaner, password)
    |> visit("/field/jobs/#{job.id}")
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-in-button']"))
    |> attach_file(css("input[name='after_photo']"),
      path: Path.expand("../support/fixtures/files/test_photo.png", __DIR__)
    )
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "photo attached"))
    |> click(css("[data-test^='checklist-item-']"))
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-out-button']"))
    |> click(css("[data-test='mark-complete-button']"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Complete"))

    # Owner: invoice shows proof of work, charge card, webhook -> Paid
    invoice = Billing.list_invoices(account_with_owner_and_cleaner_scope(owner)) |> hd()

    owner_session
    |> visit("/invoices/#{invoice.id}")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Proof of Work"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Wipe countertops"))
    |> click(button("Charge card on file"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Charge Pending"))

    payment = CleanerCrm.Repo.get_by!(CleanerCrm.Billing.Payment, invoice_id: invoice.id)

    Req.post!("http://localhost:4002/webhooks/stripe",
      json: %{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded", "data" => %{"object" => %{"id" => payment.stripe_payment_intent_id}}}
    )

    owner_session
    |> visit("/invoices/#{invoice.id}")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Paid"))
  end

  # Journey fixtures build a scope up front; re-derive an equivalent
  # scope here (rather than threading it through every assertion
  # above) purely to query the account's jobs/invoices for their ids.
  defp account_with_owner_and_cleaner_scope(owner) do
    CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(CleanerCrm.Repo.reload!(owner))
    |> then(fn scope ->
      [account] = CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts(scope)
      %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.NewClientToPaidInvoiceTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 1 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): a cleaning business
  owner takes a client from first contact through a paid invoice —
  client -> property -> checklist template -> quote -> job -> the
  cleaner's checklist proof -> invoice -> payment. Two actors, so two
  browser sessions (`@sessions 2`) rather than juggling one session's
  cookies between owner and cleaner.

  Not async: the Stripe webhook step hits the endpoint directly with
  `Req` (not through the browser), which only shares the sandboxed
  transaction correctly under `{:shared, self()}` mode — enabled when
  `async: false` (see `Wallaby.Feature`'s setup).

  Native `<input type="date">`/`<input type="time">` fields are set
  via `execute_script` (dispatching real `input`/`change` events)
  rather than `fill_in`, because segmented date/time widgets don't
  reliably accept `send_keys` text across browsers — the same
  workaround this journey needed manually during QA.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling

  @sessions 2

  feature "client to property to template to quote to job to invoice to paid", %{
    sessions: [owner_session, cleaner_session]
  } do
    %{owner: owner, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} = account_with_owner_and_cleaner()

    owner_session = log_in(owner_session, owner, password)

    owner_session =
      owner_session
      |> visit("/clients/new")
      |> fill_in(text_field("Name"), with: "Journey1 QA Client")
      |> click(checkbox("Card on file"))
      |> click(button("Save Client"))
      |> assert_has(css("h1", text: "Journey1 QA Client"))
      |> click(link("Add Property"))
      |> fill_in(text_field("Service Address"), with: "742 Evergreen Terrace")
      |> fill_in(text_field("Lockbox Code"), with: "4517")
      |> fill_in(text_field("Pet Notes"), with: "Friendly dog (Max)")
      |> click(button("Save Property"))
      |> assert_has(css("body", text: "742 Evergreen Terrace"))

    property_id = owner_session |> current_path_last_segment()

    owner_session =
      owner_session
      |> visit("/quality/templates/new")
      |> fill_in(text_field("Name"), with: "Journey1 Standard Clean")
      |> click(option("742 Evergreen Terrace"))
      |> click(css("[data-test='add-template-item-button'] input"))
      |> fill_in(css("input[placeholder='Kitchen']"), with: "Kitchen")
      |> fill_in(css("input[placeholder='Counters wiped down']"), with: "Wipe countertops")
      |> click(button("Save Template"))
      |> assert_has(css("table", text: "Journey1 Standard Clean"))

    owner_session
    |> visit("/quotes/new")
    |> fill_in(text_field("Client name"), with: "Journey1 QA Client")
    |> click(option("Per room"))
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='quote[bedroom_count]']"), with: "2")
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='quote[bathroom_count]']"), with: "1")
    |> click(css("[data-test='send-quote-button']"))
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='quote-status']", text: "Sent"))

    today = Date.utc_today() |> Date.to_iso8601()

    owner_session
    |> visit("/schedule/jobs/new")
    |> click(option("742 Evergreen Terrace"))
    |> set_native_field("input[name='job[date]']", today)
    |> set_native_field("input[name='job[start_time]']", "09:00:00")
    |> set_native_field("input[name='job[end_time]']", "11:00:00")
    |> click(option("Hourly"))
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='job[agreed_price]']"), with: "80")
    |> fill_in(css("input[name='job[hourly_rate]']"), with: "25")
    |> click(option(cleaner.email))
    |> click(css("[data-test='save-job-button']"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "scheduled"))

    scope = account_scope(owner)
    job = Scheduling.list_jobs(scope) |> Enum.find(&(&1.property_id == property_id))

    cleaner_session
    |> log_in(cleaner, password)
    |> visit("/field/jobs/#{job.id}")
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-in-button']"))
    |> attach_file(css("input[name='after_photo']"),
      path: Path.expand("../support/fixtures/files/test_photo.png", __DIR__)
    )
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "photo attached"))
    |> click(css("[data-test^='checklist-item-']"))
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-out-button']"))
    |> click(css("[data-test='mark-complete-button']"))
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test*='Complete'], .badge", text: "Complete"))

    invoice = Billing.list_invoices(scope) |> hd()

    owner_session
    |> visit("/invoices/#{invoice.id}")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Proof of Work"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Wipe countertops"))
    |> click(button("Charge card on file"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Charge Pending"))

    payment = CleanerCrm.Repo.get_by!(CleanerCrm.Billing.Payment, invoice_id: invoice.id)

    Req.post!("http://localhost:4002/webhooks/stripe",
      json: %{
        "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded",
        "data" => %{"object" => %{"id" => payment.stripe_payment_intent_id}}
      }
    )

    owner_session
    |> visit("/invoices/#{invoice.id}")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Paid"))
  end

  defp account_scope(owner) do
    scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(CleanerCrm.Repo.reload!(owner))
    [account] = CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts(scope)
    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp current_path_last_segment(session) do
    Wallaby.Browser.current_url(session) |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
  end

  defp set_native_field(session, css_selector, value) do
    Wallaby.Browser.execute_script(
      session,
      """
      var el = document.querySelector(arguments[0]);
      el.value = arguments[1];
      el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}));
      el.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      """,
      [css_selector, value]
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.JourneyFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared prerequisite setup for `test/journeys/` feature tests: an
  owner and a cleaner, both with a known password, sharing one
  account — the minimum every journey needs before it can log in
  through the browser and drive the rest of the flow for real.
  """

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Returns `%{owner:, cleaner:, account:, owner_scope:, password:}`.

  `owner` and `cleaner` both have `password` set (from
  `valid_user_password/0`) so a Wallaby session can log in as either
  through the real `/users/log-in` form.
  """
  def account_with_owner_and_cleaner(attrs \\ %{}) do
    owner = user_fixture() |> set_password()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(
        owner_scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Journey QA Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    owner_scope = %{owner_scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}

    cleaner = user_fixture() |> set_password()
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id, :member)

    %{
      owner: owner,
      cleaner: cleaner,
      account: account,
      owner_scope: owner_scope,
      password: valid_user_password()
    }
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given user into the Wallaby `session` via the real password
  form. Each actor in a multi-actor journey test should get their own
  session (via `@sessions N` / `%{sessions: [...]}`) rather than
  logging out and back in on one session — Wallaby has no cookie-clear
  helper, and juggling one session between actors doesn't match how
  two real people would use the app at once anyway.
  """
  def log_in(session, user, password) do
    import Wallaby.Query

    session
    |> Wallaby.Browser.visit("/users/log-in")
    |> Wallaby.Browser.fill_in(css("#login_form_password_email"), with: user.email)
    |> Wallaby.Browser.fill_in(css("#user_password"), with: password)
    |> Wallaby.Browser.click(button("Log in only this time"))
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.JourneyFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared prerequisite setup for `test/journeys/` feature tests: an
  owner and a cleaner, both with a known password, sharing one
  account — the minimum every journey needs before it can log in
  through the browser and drive the rest of the flow for real.
  """

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import Wallaby.Browser

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Returns `%{owner:, cleaner:, account:, owner_scope:, password:}`.

  `owner` and `cleaner` both have `password` set (from
  `valid_user_password/0`) so a Wallaby session can log in as either
  through the real `/users/log-in` form.
  """
  def account_with_owner_and_cleaner(attrs \\ %{}) do
    owner = user_fixture() |> set_password()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(
        owner_scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Journey QA Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    owner_scope = %{owner_scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}

    cleaner = user_fixture() |> set_password()
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id, :member)

    %{
      owner: owner,
      cleaner: cleaner,
      account: account,
      owner_scope: owner_scope,
      password: valid_user_password()
    }
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given user into the Wallaby `session` via the real password
  form. Each actor in a multi-actor journey test should get their own
  session (via `@sessions N` / `%{sessions: [...]}`) rather than
  logging out and back in on one session — Wallaby has no cookie-clear
  helper, and juggling one session between actors doesn't match how
  two real people would use the app at once anyway.
  """
  def log_in(session, user, password) do
    import Wallaby.Query

    session
    |> visit("/users/log-in")
    |> assert_has(css(".phx-connected"))
    |> fill_in(css("#login_form_password_email"), with: user.email)
    |> fill_in(css("#user_password"), with: password)
    |> click(button("Log in only this time"))
    |> assert_has(css(".phx-connected"))
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserSessionController do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  def create(conn, %{"_action" => "confirmed"} = params) do
    create(conn, params, "User confirmed successfully.")
  end

  def create(conn, params) do
    create(conn, params, "Welcome back!")
  end

  # magic link login
  defp create(conn, %{"user" => %{"token" => token} = user_params}, info) do
    case Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token) do
      {:ok, {user, tokens_to_disconnect}} ->
        UserAuth.disconnect_sessions(tokens_to_disconnect)

        conn
        |> put_flash(:info, info)
        |> UserAuth.log_in_user(user, user_params)

      _ ->
        conn
        |> put_flash(:error, "The link is invalid or it has expired.")
        |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
    end
  end

  # email + password login
  defp create(conn, %{"user" => user_params}, info) do
    %{"email" => email, "password" => password} = user_params

    if user = Users.get_user_by_email_and_password(email, password) do
      conn
      |> put_flash(:info, info)
      |> UserAuth.log_in_user(user, user_params)
    else
      # In order to prevent user enumeration attacks, don't disclose whether the email is registered.
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "Invalid email or password")
      |> put_flash(:email, String.slice(email, 0, 160))
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
    end
  end

  def update_password(conn, %{"user" => user_params} = params) do
    user = conn.assigns.current_scope.user
    true = Users.sudo_mode?(user)
    {:ok, {_user, expired_tokens}} = Users.update_user_password(user, user_params)

    # disconnect all existing LiveViews with old sessions
    UserAuth.disconnect_sessions(expired_tokens)

    conn
    |> put_session(:user_return_to, ~p"/users/settings")
    |> create(params, "Password updated successfully!")
  end

  def delete(conn, _params) do
    conn
    |> put_flash(:info, "Logged out successfully.")
    |> UserAuth.log_out_user()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.JourneyFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared prerequisite setup for `test/journeys/` feature tests: an
  owner and a cleaner, both with a known password, sharing one
  account — the minimum every journey needs before it can log in
  through the browser and drive the rest of the flow for real.
  """

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import Wallaby.Browser

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Returns `%{owner:, cleaner:, account:, owner_scope:, password:}`.

  `owner` and `cleaner` both have `password` set (from
  `valid_user_password/0`) so a Wallaby session can log in as either
  through the real `/users/log-in` form.
  """
  def account_with_owner_and_cleaner(attrs \\ %{}) do
    owner = user_fixture() |> set_password()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(
        owner_scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Journey QA Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    owner_scope = %{owner_scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}

    cleaner = user_fixture() |> set_password()
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id, :member)

    %{
      owner: owner,
      cleaner: cleaner,
      account: account,
      owner_scope: owner_scope,
      password: valid_user_password()
    }
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given user into the Wallaby `session` via the real password
  form. Each actor in a multi-actor journey test should get their own
  session (via `@sessions N` / `%{sessions: [...]}`) rather than
  logging out and back in on one session — Wallaby has no cookie-clear
  helper, and juggling one session between actors doesn't match how
  two real people would use the app at once anyway.
  """
  def log_in(session, user, password) do
    import Wallaby.Query

    session
    |> visit("/users/log-in")
    |> assert_has(css(".phx-connected"))
    |> fill_in(css("#login_form_password_email"), with: user.email)
    |> fill_in(css("#user_password"), with: password)
    |> click(button("Log in only this time"))
    # The password form submits over the LiveView socket first, which
    # just flips `phx-trigger-action` to make the JS client re-submit
    # it a second time as a real native POST (the only way to actually
    # write the session cookie) — that second, real submission is
    # what redirects and is what we need to wait for here, not the
    # socket round-trip the click itself waits on.
    |> assert_has(link("Log out"))
  end
end

@doc """
  Logs the given user into the Wallaby `session` via the real password
  form. Each actor in a multi-actor journey test should get their own
  session (via `@sessions N` / `%{sessions: [...]}`) rather than
  logging out and back in on one session — Wallaby has no cookie-clear
  helper, and juggling one session between actors doesn't match how
  two real people would use the app at once anyway.

  Two timing quirks, both confirmed by repeated runs, not guesses:

  - The magic-link form's email input carries `phx-mounted={JS.focus()}`
    (autofocus on connect). If the password form's email field is
    filled before that hook fires, the steal-focus race sometimes
    empties it back out mid-keystroke — so this waits a beat after
    `visit` before touching either field.
  - The password form submits over the LiveView socket first, which
    just flips `phx-trigger-action` to make the JS client re-submit it
    a second time as a real native POST (the only way to actually
    write the session cookie) — so this waits for something that only
    exists after that second, real submission lands, not just for the
    click's own socket round-trip.
  """
  def log_in(session, user, password) do
    import Wallaby.Query

    session = visit(session, "/users/log-in")
    Process.sleep(500)

    session
    |> fill_in(css("#login_form_password_email"), with: user.email)
    |> fill_in(css("#user_password"), with: password)
    |> click(button("Log in only this time"))
    |> assert_has(link("Log out"))
  end
end

    Wallaby.Browser.execute_script(
      session,
      """
      var el = document.querySelector(arguments[0]);
      el.checked = true;
      el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}));
      el.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
      """,
      [css_selector]
    )
  end

  # on the login page's real POST-resubmit). An explicit settle beat

  defp settle(session) do
    Process.sleep(600)
    session
  end
