Two actors, so two browser sessions (`@sessions 2`) rather than juggling one session's cookies between owner and cleaner. Not async: the Stripe webhook step hits the endpoint directly with `Req` (not through the browser), which only shares the sandboxed transaction correctly under `{:shared, self()}` mode — enabled when `async: false` (see `Wallaby.Feature`'s setup). Fields are set via `set_field/3` (JS `.value` + a real `input`/ `change` event dispatch) rather than `fill_in`/label-text queries — this form's `` markup isn't one Wallaby's label-lookup resolves, and native `` widgets don't reliably accept `send_keys` text across browsers regardless. Both were confirmed reliable manually during QA before being ported here. """ use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false alias CleanerCrm.Billing alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling @sessions 2 feature "client to property to template to quote to job to invoice to paid", %{ sessions: [owner_session, cleaner_session] } do %{owner: owner, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} = account_with_owner_and_cleaner() owner_session = log_in(owner_session, owner, password) owner_session = owner_session |> visit("/clients/new") |> set_field("#client_name", "Journey1 QA Client") |> check_field("#client_card_on_file") |> click(button("Save Client")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("h1", text: "Journey1 QA Client")) |> click(link("Add Property")) |> set_field("#property_service_address", "742 Evergreen Terrace") |> set_field("#property_lockbox_code", "4517") |> set_field("#property_pet_notes", "Friendly dog (Max)") |> click(button("Save Property")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("body", text: "742 Evergreen Terrace")) property_id = current_path_last_segment(owner_session) owner_session = owner_session |> visit("/quality/templates/new") |> set_field("#template_name", "Journey1 Standard Clean") |> set_field("#template_property_id", property_id) |> check_field("[data-test='add-template-item-button'] input") |> settle() |> set_field("input[placeholder='Kitchen']", "Kitchen") |> set_field("input[placeholder='Counters wiped down']", "Wipe countertops") |> click(button("Save Template")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("table", text: "Journey1 Standard Clean")) owner_session |> visit("/quotes/new") |> set_field("input[name='quote[client_name]']", "Journey1 QA Client") |> set_field("select[name='quote[pricing_model]']", "per_room") |> settle() |> set_field("input[name='quote[bedroom_count]']", "2") |> set_field("input[name='quote[bathroom_count]']", "1") |> click(css("[data-test='send-quote-button']")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("[data-test='quote-status']", text: "Sent")) today = Date.utc_today() |> Date.to_iso8601() owner_session |> visit("/schedule/jobs/new") |> set_field("select[name='job[property_id]']", property_id) |> set_field("input[name='job[date]']", today) |> set_field("input[name='job[start_time]']", "09:00:00") |> set_field("input[name='job[end_time]']", "11:00:00") |> set_field("select[name='job[pay_type]']", "hourly") |> set_field("input[name='job[agreed_price]']", "80") |> set_field("input[name='job[hourly_rate]']", "25") |> set_field("select[name='job[cleaner_id]']", to_string(cleaner.id)) |> click(css("[data-test='save-job-button']")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("body", text: "scheduled")) scope = account_scope(owner) job = Scheduling.list_jobs(scope) |> Enum.find(&(&1.property_id == property_id)) cleaner_session |> log_in(cleaner, password) |> visit("/field/jobs/#{job.id}") |> click(css("[data-test='clock-in-button']")) |> settle() |> attach_file(css("input[name='after_photo']"), path: Path.expand("../support/fixtures/files/test_photo.png", __DIR__) ) |> assert_has(css("body", text: "photo attached")) |> click(css("[data-test^='checklist-item-']")) |> settle() |> click(css("[data-test='clock-out-button']")) |> settle() |> click(css("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Complete")) invoice = Billing.list_invoices(scope) |> hd() owner_session |> visit("/invoices/#{invoice.id}") |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Proof of Work")) |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Wipe countertops")) |> click(button("Charge card on file")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Charge Pending")) payment = CleanerCrm.Repo.get_by!(CleanerCrm.Billing.Payment, invoice_id: invoice.id) Req.post!("http://localhost:4002/webhooks/stripe", json: %{ "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded", "data" => %{"object" => %{"id" => payment.stripe_payment_intent_id}} } ) owner_session |> visit("/invoices/#{invoice.id}") |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Paid")) end defp account_scope(owner) do scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(CleanerCrm.Repo.reload!(owner)) [account] = CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts(scope) %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id} end defp current_path_last_segment(session) do Wallaby.Browser.current_url(session) |> String.split("/") |> List.last() end defp set_field(session, css_selector, value) do Wallaby.Browser.execute_script( session, """ var el = document.querySelector(arguments[0]); el.value = arguments[1]; el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); el.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true})); """, [css_selector, value] ) end defp check_field(session, css_selector) do Wallaby.Browser.execute_script( session, """ var el = document.querySelector(arguments[0]); el.checked = true; el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); el.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true})); """, [css_selector] ) end # # guess (see `log_in/3` in journey_fixtures.ex for the same pattern # on the login page's real POST-resubmit). current_path_last_segment(owner_session) owner_session = owner_session |> visit!("/quality/templates/new") |> set_field("#template_name", "Journey1 Standard Clean") |> set_field("#template_property_id", property_id) |> check_field("[data-test='add-template-item-button'] input") |> settle() |> set_field("input[placeholder='Kitchen']", "Kitchen") |> set_field("input[placeholder='Counters wiped down']", "Wipe countertops") |> click(button("Save Template")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("table", text: "Journey1 Standard Clean")) owner_session |> visit!("/quotes/new") |> set_field("#rate_card_per_room_bedroom_rate_cents", "5000") |> set_field("#rate_card_per_room_bathroom_rate_cents", "3000") |> click(button("Save Rate Card")) |> settle() |> |> set_field("input[name='quote[bathroom_count]']", "1") |> settle() |> click(css("[data-test='send-quote-button']")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("[data-test='quote-status']", text: "Sent")) today = Date.utc_today() |> Date.to_iso8601() owner_session |> visit!("/schedule/jobs/new") |> set_field("select[name='job[property_id]']", property_id) |> set_field("input[name='job[date]']", today) |> set_field("input[name='job[start_time]']", "09:00:00") |> set_field("input[name='job[end_time]']", "11:00:00") |> set_field("select[name='job[pay_type]']", "hourly") |> set_field("input[name='job[agreed_price]']", "80") |> set_field("input[name='job[hourly_rate]']", "25") |> set_field("select[name='job[cleaner_id]']", to_string(cleaner.id)) |> click(button("Save Job")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("body", text: "scheduled")) scope = account_scope(owner) job = Scheduling.list_jobs(scope) |> Enum.find(&(&1.property_id == property_id)) cleaner_session |> log_in(cleaner, password) |> visit!("/field/jobs/#{job.id}") |> click(css("[data-test='clock-in-button']")) |> settle() |> attach_file(css("input[name='after_photo']"), path: Path.expand("../support/fixtures/files/test_photo.png", __DIR__) ) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("body", text: "photo attached")) |> click(css("[data-test^='checklist-item-']")) |> settle() |> click(css("[data-test='clock-out-button']")) |> settle() |> click(css("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")) |> settle() |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Complete")) invoice = visit!("/invoices/#{invoice.id}") |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Paid")) end defp account_scope(owner) do scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(CleanerCrm.Repo.reload!(owner)) [account] = CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts(scope) %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id} end defp current_path_last_segment(session) do Wallaby.Browser.current_url(session) |> defp pending?(%{entries: entries}), do: Enum.any?(entries, &(not &1.done?))

  @impl true
  def mount(socket) do
    {:ok,
     socket
     |> assign(:in_flight_photos, %{})
     |> allow_upload(:before_photo,
       accept: ~w(.jpg .jpeg .png),
       max_entries: 1,
       auto_upload: true,
       progress: &handle_progress/3
     )
     |> allow_upload(:after_photo,
       accept: ~w(.jpg .jpeg .png),
       max_entries: 1,
       auto_upload: true,
       progress: &handle_progress/3
     )}
  end

  @impl true
  def update(assigns, socket) do
    {:ok, assign(socket, assigns)}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_event("toggle", _params, socket) do
    {:ok, _item} =
      Quality.toggle_checklist_item(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.item)

    notify_checklist_changed()
    {:noreply, socket}
  end

  def handle_event("noop", _params, socket), do: {:noreply, socket}

  # A `Photo` row is created `:pending` on the first progress callback
  # for a given upload — before any bytes have landed — and flipped to
  # `:uploaded` once the entry finishes. `in_flight_photos` remembers
  # which row belongs to this upload for the rest of this component's
  # lifetime, so a later chunk reuses it rather than creating a
  # duplicate; a fresh mount (after a dropped connection) instead finds
  # the still-pending row via `existing_pending_photo/2`.
  defp handle_progress(kind, entry, socket) do
    {socket, photo} = ensure_pending_photo(socket, kind)

    socket =
      if entry.done? do
        scope = socket.assigns.current_scope

        storage_key =
          consume_uploaded_entry(socket, entry, fn %{path: path} ->
            {:ok, store_upload!(path, entry)}
          end)

        {:ok, _photo} = Quality.complete_photo_upload(scope, photo, storage_key)

        notify_checklist_changed()
        assign(socket, :in_flight_photos, Map.delete(socket.assigns.in_flight_photos, kind))
      else
        socket
      end

    {:noreply, socket}
  end

  defp ensure_pending_photo(socket, kind) do
    case Map.get(socket.assigns.in_flight_photos, kind) do
      nil ->
        scope = socket.assigns.current_scope
        item = socket.assigns.item
        photo_kind = photo_kind(kind)

        photo =
          existing_pending_photo(item, photo_kind) ||
            create_pending_photo!(scope, item, photo_kind)

        {assign(socket, :in_flight_photos, Map.put(socket.assigns.in_flight_photos, kind, photo)),
         photo}

      photo ->
        {socket, photo}
    end
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.JourneyFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared prerequisite setup for `test/journeys/` feature tests: an
  owner and a cleaner, both with a known password, sharing one
  account — the minimum every journey needs before it can log in
  through the browser and drive the rest of the flow for real.
  """

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import Wallaby.Browser

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Returns `%{owner:, cleaner:, account:, owner_scope:, password:}`.

  `owner` and `cleaner` both have `password` set (from
  `valid_user_password/0`) so a Wallaby session can log in as either
  through the real `/users/log-in` form.
  """
  def account_with_owner_and_cleaner(attrs \\ %{}) do
    owner = user_fixture() |> set_password()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(
        owner_scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Journey QA Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    owner_scope = %{owner_scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}

    cleaner = user_fixture() |> set_password()
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id, :member)

    %{
      owner: owner,
      cleaner: cleaner,
      account: account,
      owner_scope: owner_scope,
      password: valid_user_password()
    }
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given user into the Wallaby `session` via the real password
  form. Each actor in a multi-actor journey test should get their own
  session (via `@sessions N` / `%{sessions: [...]}`) rather than
  logging out and back in on one session — Wallaby has no cookie-clear
  helper, and juggling one session between actors doesn't match how
  two real people would use the app at once anyway.

  Two timing quirks, both confirmed by repeated runs, not guesses:

  - The magic-link form's email input carries `phx-mounted={JS.focus()}`
    (autofocus on connect). If the password form's email field is
    filled before that hook fires, the steal-focus race sometimes
    empties it back out mid-keystroke — so this waits a beat after
    `visit` before touching either field.
  - The password form submits over the LiveView socket first, which
    just flips `phx-trigger-action` to make the JS client re-submit it
    a second time as a real native POST (the only way to actually
    write the session cookie) — so this waits for something that only
    exists after that second, real submission lands, not just for the
    click's own socket round-trip.
  """
  def log_in(session, user, password) do
    import Wallaby.Query

    session = visit(session, "/users/log-in")
    Process.sleep(500)

    session
    |> fill_in(css("#login_form_password_email"), with: user.email)
    |> fill_in(css("#user_password"), with: password)
    |> click(button("Log in only this time"))
    |> assert_has(link("Log out"))
  end
end

  helper, and juggling one session between actors doesn't match how
  two real people would use the app at once anyway.

  - The magic-link form's email input carries `phx-mounted={JS.focus()}`
    (autofocus on connect). If the password form's email field is
    filled before that hook fires, the steal-focus race sometimes
    empties it back out mid-keystroke — so this waits a beat after
    `visit` before touching either field.
  - The password form submits over the LiveView socket first, which
    just flips `phx-trigger-action` to make the JS client re-submit it
    a second time as a real native POST (the only way to actually
    write the session cookie) — so this waits for something that only
    exists after that second, real submission lands, not just for the
    click's own socket round-trip.
  """
  def log_in(session, user, password) do
    import Wallaby.Query

    session = visit(session, "/users/log-in")
    Process.sleep(500)

    session
    |> fill_in(css("#login_form_password_email"), with: user.email)
    |> fill_in(css("#user_password"), with: password)
    |> click(button("Log in only this time"))
    |> assert_has(link("Log out"))
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.CleanerDayTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 2 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): a cleaner works an
  entire day inside `/field` — today's jobs in order, a full
  get-in-the-door brief, clocking in/out, working a room-by-room
  checklist, filing an incident report, and being fenced out of every
  office-only surface and every other cleaner's job.

  Client/property/template/job setup goes through context functions
  directly (not the browser) — Journey 1 already regression-tests
  that authoring path; this journey's subject is the cleaner's day,
  not how the office built the job.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling

  @sessions 2

  feature "a cleaner's full day, plus the isolation it can't cross", %{
    sessions: [cleaner_session, other_cleaner_session]
  } do
    %{owner_scope: scope, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} = account_with_owner_and_cleaner()
    other_cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account) |> set_password_for()

    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Journey2 QA Client"})

    property =
      property_fixture(scope, client, %{
        service_address: "12 Field Lane",
        entry_method: "Lockbox on gate",
        lockbox_code: "7788",
        pet_notes: "Two cats, keep indoors"
      })

    {:ok, template} =
      Quality.create_checklist_template(scope, %{
        name: "Journey2 Template",
        property_id: property.id,
        items: [
          %{room: "Kitchen", task: "Wipe counters", required: true},
          %{room: "Bathroom", task: "Scrub tub", required: true}
        ]
      })

    job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        pay_type: :hourly,
        hourly_rate_cents: 2500
      })

    other_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: other_cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
        start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[15:00:00]
      })

    cleaner_session = log_in(cleaner_session, cleaner, password)

    cleaner_session
    |> visit!("/field")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "12 Field Lane"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Lockbox on gate"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "7788"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Two cats, keep indoors"))
    |> refute_has(css("body", text: "13:00"))

    cleaner_session
    |> visit!("/field/jobs/#{job.id}")
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-in-button']"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='elapsed-time']"))

    template_item_ids =
      CleanerCrm.Repo.all(
        CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistItem
        |> Ecto.Query.where([i], i.task in ["Wipe counters", "Scrub tub"])
      )
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1.checklist_id in checklist_ids_for(scope, job)))
      |> Enum.map(& &1.id)

    Enum.reduce(template_item_ids, cleaner_session, fn item_id, session ->
      session
      |> click(css("[data-test='checklist-item-#{item_id}']"))
      |> settle()
    end)

    cleaner_session
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='checklist-progress']", text: "2 of 2"))
    |> set_field("#incident_type", "unsafe_condition")
    |> set_field("#incident_description", "Frayed cord near the outlet.")
    |> click(button("File Report"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='incident-report-item']", text: "Frayed cord near the outlet."))
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-out-button']"))
    |> settle()
    |> click(css("[data-test='mark-complete-button']"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Complete"))

    cleaner_session
    |> visit!("/field")
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='job-earnings']"))

    cleaner_session
    |> visit(~s"/field/jobs/#{other_job.id}")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "not assigned to you"))

    cleaner_session
    |> visit("/schedule")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "don't have access"))

    cleaner_session
    |> visit("/timesheets")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "don't have access"))

    # `other_cleaner_session` only exists so the second cleaner is a
    # real logged-in actor while the isolation checks above run — no
    # separate assertions of its own needed.
    log_in(other_cleaner_session, other_cleaner, password)
  end

  defp checklist_ids_for(scope, job) do
    case Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil -> []
      checklist -> [checklist.id]
    end
  end

  defp set_password_for(user), do: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.set_password(user)
end

Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
  """
  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id and c.job_id == ^job_id)
    |> preload(items: :photos)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  @doc """
  Groups a checklist's items by room, in the order each room first
  appears. Items with no room (a flat, unrouted checklist) are
  grouped under `nil`.
  """
  def group_by_room(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    rooms = Enum.uniq_by(items, & &1.room) |> Enum.map(& &1.room)
    grouped = Enum.group_by(items, & &1.room)
    Enum.map(rooms, &{&1, Map.fetch!(grouped, &1)})
  end

  @doc "`{checked_count, total_count}` across a checklist's items."
  def progress(%Checklist{items: items}), do: {Enum.count(items, & &1.checked), length(items)}

  @doc """
  Toggles a checklist item's checked state. Checking an item clears
  any prior skip.
  """
  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{checked: true} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.uncheck_changeset() |> Repo.update()

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.CleanerDayTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 2 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): a cleaner works an
  entire day inside `/field` — today's jobs in order, a full
  get-in-the-door brief, clocking in/out, working a room-by-room
  checklist, filing an incident report, and being fenced out of every
  office-only surface and every other cleaner's job.

  Client/property/template/job setup goes through context functions
  directly (not the browser) — Journey 1 already regression-tests
  that authoring path; this journey's subject is the cleaner's day,
  not how the office built the job.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling

  @sessions 2

  feature "a cleaner's full day, plus the isolation it can't cross", %{
    sessions: [cleaner_session, other_cleaner_session]
  } do
    %{owner_scope: scope, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} = account_with_owner_and_cleaner()
    other_cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account) |> set_password_for()

    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Journey2 QA Client"})

    property =
      property_fixture(scope, client, %{
        service_address: "12 Field Lane",
        entry_method: "Lockbox on gate",
        lockbox_code: "7788",
        pet_notes: "Two cats, keep indoors"
      })

    {:ok, template} =
      Quality.create_checklist_template(scope, %{
        name: "Journey2 Template",
        property_id: property.id,
        items: [
          %{room: "Kitchen", task: "Wipe counters", required: true},
          %{room: "Bathroom", task: "Scrub tub", required: true}
        ]
      })

    job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        pay_type: :hourly,
        hourly_rate_cents: 2500
      })

    other_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: other_cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
        start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[15:00:00]
      })

    cleaner_session = log_in(cleaner_session, cleaner, password)

    cleaner_session
    |> visit!("/field")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "12 Field Lane"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Lockbox on gate"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "7788"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Two cats, keep indoors"))
    |> refute_has(css("body", text: "13:00"))

    cleaner_session
    |> visit!("/field/jobs/#{job.id}")
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-in-button']"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='elapsed-time']"))

    checklist = Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job)

    Enum.reduce(checklist.items, cleaner_session, fn item, session ->
      session
      |> click(css("[data-test='checklist-item-#{item.id}']"))
      |> settle()
    end)

    cleaner_session
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='checklist-progress']", text: "2 of 2"))
    |> set_field("#incident_type", "unsafe_condition")
    |> set_field("#incident_description", "Frayed cord near the outlet.")
    |> click(button("File Report"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='incident-report-item']", text: "Frayed cord near the outlet."))
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-out-button']"))
    |> settle()
    |> click(css("[data-test='mark-complete-button']"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Complete"))

    cleaner_session
    |> visit!("/field")
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='job-earnings']"))

    cleaner_session
    |> visit(~s"/field/jobs/#{other_job.id}")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "not assigned to you"))

    cleaner_session
    |> visit("/schedule")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "don't have access"))

    cleaner_session
    |> visit("/timesheets")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "don't have access"))

    # `other_cleaner_session` only exists so the second cleaner is a
    # real logged-in actor while the isolation checks above run — no
    # separate assertions of its own needed.
    log_in(other_cleaner_session, other_cleaner, password)
  end

  defp checklist_ids_for(scope, job) do
    case Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil -> []
      checklist -> [checklist.id]
    end
  end

  defp set_password_for(user), do: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.set_password(user)
end

      |> settle()

    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='checklist-progress']", text: "2 of 2"))
    |> set_field("#incident_type", "unsafe_condition")

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.CleanerDayTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 2 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): a cleaner works an
  entire day inside `/field` — today's jobs in order, a full
  get-in-the-door brief, clocking in/out, working a room-by-room
  checklist, filing an incident report, and being fenced out of every
  office-only surface and every other cleaner's job.

  Client/property/template/job setup goes through context functions
  directly (not the browser) — Journey 1 already regression-tests
  that authoring path; this journey's subject is the cleaner's day,
  not how the office built the job. Only one browser actor is needed:
  the "other cleaner" whose job we must not be able to open is just a
  fixture record, never logged in anywhere.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality

  feature "a cleaner's full day, plus the isolation it can't cross", %{session: session} do
    %{owner_scope: scope, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} = account_with_owner_and_cleaner()
    other_cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Journey2 QA Client"})

    property =
      property_fixture(scope, client, %{
        service_address: "12 Field Lane",
        entry_method: "Lockbox on gate",
        lockbox_code: "7788",
        pet_notes: "Two cats, keep indoors"
      })

    {:ok, _template} =
      Quality.create_checklist_template(scope, %{
        name: "Journey2 Template",
        property_id: property.id,
        items: [
          %{room: "Kitchen", task: "Wipe counters", required: true},
          %{room: "Bathroom", task: "Scrub tub", required: true}
        ]
      })

    job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        pay_type: :hourly,
        hourly_rate_cents: 2500
      })

    other_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: other_cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
        start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[15:00:00]
      })

    session = log_in(session, cleaner, password)

    session
    |> visit!("/field")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "12 Field Lane"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Lockbox on gate"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "7788"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Two cats, keep indoors"))
    |> refute_has(css("body", text: "13:00"))
    |> visit!("/field/jobs/#{job.id}")
    |> click(css("[data-test='clock-in-button']"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='elapsed-time']"))

    checklist = Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job)

    session =
      Enum.reduce(checklist.items, session, fn item, s ->
        s |> click(css("[data-test='checklist-item-#{item.id}']")) |> settle()
      end)

    session

input.title: Completing a job with no agreed_price_cents crashes invoice generation (NOT NULL violation) — reachable via recurring plans, which never set a price
input.description:
Found while writing the Journey 2 Wallaby test (test/journeys/cleaner_day_test.exs, "a cleaner's full day"): a job created with `agreed_price_cents: nil` and marked complete via the field UI (`mark_complete` in `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`, checklist_component.ex:168) crashes the LiveView process with:

```
** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 23502 (not_null_violation) null value in column "amount_cents" of relation "invoices" violates not-null constraint
```

Root cause: `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job.changeset/2` (lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling/job.ex:82-88) does NOT include `agreed_price_cents` in `validate_required`, so the schema happily persists a job with no price. But invoice generation (triggered from `mark_complete`) apparently derives `invoices.amount_cents` directly from the job's `agreed_price_cents` with no fallback/guard, so any such job crashes on completion instead of failing gracefully or defaulting sensibly.

This isn't just a contrived test fixture gap — it's genuinely reachable in normal use: `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1` (lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling/recurrence.ex:46-55), which materializes every visit for a recurring plan (the whole subject of Journey 4, "preferred cleaner continuity"), builds its job attrs map with `property_id`, `cleaner_id`, `recurring_plan_id`, `scheduled_date`, `start_time`, `end_time` — no `agreed_price_cents` at all, because the recurring-plan form (`/schedule/plans/new`) has no price field. So any job materialized from a recurring plan and carried through to completion (clock in/out, finish checklist, mark complete) will hit this exact crash. Journey 4's QA never completed a materialized visit end-to-end (it only tested reassignment/warnings), so this went unnoticed there.

Suggested fix: either require `agreed_price_cents` at the point a job becomes eligible for completion (validate before allowing clock-in/mark-complete, with a friendly "set a price before finishing this job" message), or have invoice generation default a missing price to 0 rather than crash, or require recurring plans to also capture a price so materialized jobs are never priceless in the first place.

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.ScheduleChaosTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 3 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): reminders, reschedules,
  cancellations, and the audit trail that reconstructs all of it.
  Confirming/rescheduling/cancelling all happen through the real
  `/schedule` board; the escalation-window backdate is done directly
  through `Repo` here (this test's equivalent of the sanctioned psql
  step from manual QA — same idea, same effect, just against the
  sandboxed test DB instead of dev).
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications

  @sessions 2

  feature "reminders, reschedule/cancel alerts, acknowledgment, escalation, and the audit trail",
          %{sessions: [owner_session, cleaner_session]} do
    %{owner_scope: scope, owner: owner, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} =
      account_with_owner_and_cleaner()

    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Journey3 QA Client"})
    property = property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "9 Chaos Ct"})

    today = Date.utc_today()

    reminder_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        agreed_price_cents: 8000
      })

    reminder_token = Notifications.generate_token()

    {:ok, _} =
      Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{
        job_id: reminder_job.id,
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        kind: :reminder,
        channel: :email,
        status: :sent,
        token: reminder_token
      })

    reschedule_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[15:00:00],
        agreed_price_cents: 8000
      })

    cancel_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[17:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[19:00:00],
        agreed_price_cents: 8000
      })

    owner_session = log_in(owner_session, owner, password)

    # Step 1: confirm the reminder, verify "Confirmed" on the board.
    owner_session
    |> visit!("/reminders/confirm/#{reminder_token}")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Confirmed"))
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> assert_has(job_row(reminder_job.id), text: "Confirmed")

    # Step 2: reschedule a different job's start time via the board's
    # inline time input — the one control confirmed (during manual QA)
    # to actually push a schedule-change alert.
    owner_session
    |> set_field("[data-test='job-#{reschedule_job.id}-start-time-input']", "13:30:00")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(job_row(reschedule_job.id), text: "Unacknowledged")
    |> assert_has(job_row(reschedule_job.id), text: "moved from")

    # Step 3: the cleaner sees the loud alert on /field and
    # acknowledges it; the owner's board reflects the ack.
    cleaner_session = log_in(cleaner_session, cleaner, password)

    cleaner_session
    |> visit!("/field")
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='schedule-alert']"))
    |> click(css("[data-test$='-acknowledge-button']"))
    |> settle()

    owner_session
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> assert_has(job_row(reschedule_job.id), text: "Acknowledged")

    # Step 4: cancel a job — it stays visible with a Cancelled badge
    # and Unacknowledged status.
    owner_session
    |> click(css("[data-test='job-#{cancel_job.id}'] button", text: "Cancel"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='job-#{cancel_job.id}-cancelled-badge']"))
    |> assert_has(job_row(cancel_job.id), text: "Unacknowledged")

    # Step 5: backdate the cancellation alert past the escalation
    # window (10 minutes, per CleanerCrm.Notifications) — verify it
    # flips to Escalated/SMS on next read.
    cancel_notification =
      Notifications.list_notifications(scope)
      |> Enum.find(&(&1.job_id == cancel_job.id and &1.kind == :schedule_change))

    {:ok, _} =
      cancel_notification
      |> Ecto.Changeset.change(pushed_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -700, :second))
      |> CleanerCrm.Repo.update()

    owner_session
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> assert_has(job_row(cancel_job.id), text: "Escalated")

    # Step 6: the audit trail reconstructs the reschedule and
    # cancellation, filtered by actor and record type.
    owner_session
    |> visit!("/audit")
    |> set_field("#filter_actor", owner.email)
    |> set_field("#filter_subject_type", "Job")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='audit-entries']", text: "rescheduled"))

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.ScheduleChaosTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 3 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): reminders, reschedules,
  cancellations, and the audit trail that reconstructs all of it.
  Confirming/rescheduling/cancelling all happen through the real
  `/schedule` board; the escalation-window backdate is done directly
  through `Repo` here (this test's equivalent of the sanctioned psql
  step from manual QA — same idea, same effect, just against the
  sandboxed test DB instead of dev).
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications

  @sessions 2

  feature "reminders, reschedule/cancel alerts, acknowledgment, escalation, and the audit trail",
          %{sessions: [owner_session, cleaner_session]} do
    %{owner_scope: scope, owner: owner, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} =
      account_with_owner_and_cleaner()

    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Journey3 QA Client"})
    property = property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "9 Chaos Ct"})

    today = Date.utc_today()

    reminder_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        agreed_price_cents: 8000
      })

    reminder_token = Notifications.generate_token()

    {:ok, _} =
      Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{
        job_id: reminder_job.id,
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        kind: :reminder,
        channel: :email,
        status: :sent,
        token: reminder_token
      })

    reschedule_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[15:00:00],
        agreed_price_cents: 8000
      })

    cancel_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[17:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[19:00:00],
        agreed_price_cents: 8000
      })

    owner_session = log_in(owner_session, owner, password)

    # Step 1: confirm the reminder, verify "Confirmed" on the board.
    owner_session
    |> visit!("/reminders/confirm/#{reminder_token}")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Confirmed"))
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> assert_has(job_row(reminder_job.id, "Confirmed"))

    # Step 2: reschedule a different job's start time via the board's
    # inline time input — the one control confirmed (during manual QA)
    # to actually push a schedule-change alert.
    owner_session
    |> set_field("[data-test='job-#{reschedule_job.id}-start-time-input']", "13:30:00")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(job_row(reschedule_job.id, "Unacknowledged"))
    |> assert_has(job_row(reschedule_job.id, "moved from"))

    # Step 3: the cleaner sees the loud alert on /field and
    # acknowledges it; the owner's board reflects the ack.
    cleaner_session = log_in(cleaner_session, cleaner, password)

    cleaner_session
    |> visit!("/field")
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='schedule-alert']"))
    |> click(css("[data-test$='-acknowledge-button']"))
    |> settle()

    owner_session
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> assert_has(job_row(reschedule_job.id, "Acknowledged"))

    # Step 4: cancel a job — it stays visible with a Cancelled badge
    # and Unacknowledged status.
    owner_session
    |> click(css("[data-test='job-#{cancel_job.id}'] button", text: "Cancel"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='job-#{cancel_job.id}-cancelled-badge']"))
    |> assert_has(job_row(cancel_job.id), text: "Unacknowledged")

    # Step 5: backdate the cancellation alert past the escalation
    # window (10 minutes, per CleanerCrm.Notifications) — verify it
    # flips to Escalated/SMS on next read.
    cancel_notification =
      Notifications.list_notifications(scope)
      |> Enum.find(&(&1.job_id == cancel_job.id and &1.kind == :schedule_change))

    {:ok, _} =
      cancel_notification
      |> Ecto.Changeset.change(pushed_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -700, :second))
      |> CleanerCrm.Repo.update()

    owner_session
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> assert_has(job_row(cancel_job.id), text: "Escalated")

    # Step 6: the audit trail reconstructs the reschedule and
    # cancellation, filtered by actor and record type.
    owner_session
    |> visit!("/audit")
    |> set_field("#filter_actor", owner.email)
    |> set_field("#filter_subject_type", "Job")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='audit-entries']", text: "rescheduled"))
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='audit-entries']", text: "cancelled"))
  end

  defp job_row(job_id), do: css("[data-test='job-#{job_id}']")
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.ScheduleChaosTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 3 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): reminders, reschedules,
  cancellations, and the audit trail that reconstructs all of it.
  Confirming/rescheduling/cancelling all happen through the real
  `/schedule` board; the escalation-window backdate is done directly
  through `Repo` here (this test's equivalent of the sanctioned psql
  step from manual QA — same idea, same effect, just against the
  sandboxed test DB instead of dev).
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications

  @sessions 2

  feature "reminders, reschedule/cancel alerts, acknowledgment, escalation, and the audit trail",
          %{sessions: [owner_session, cleaner_session]} do
    %{owner_scope: scope, owner: owner, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} =
      account_with_owner_and_cleaner()

    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Journey3 QA Client"})
    property = property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "9 Chaos Ct"})

    today = Date.utc_today()

    reminder_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        agreed_price_cents: 8000
      })

    reminder_token = Notifications.generate_token()

    {:ok, _} =
      Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{
        job_id: reminder_job.id,
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        kind: :reminder,
        channel: :email,
        status: :sent,
        token: reminder_token
      })

    reschedule_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[15:00:00],
        agreed_price_cents: 8000
      })

    cancel_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[17:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[19:00:00],
        agreed_price_cents: 8000
      })

    owner_session = log_in(owner_session, owner, password)

    # Step 1: confirm the reminder, verify "Confirmed" on the board.
    owner_session
    |> visit!("/reminders/confirm/#{reminder_token}")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Confirmed"))
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> assert_has(job_row(reminder_job.id, "Confirmed"))

    # Step 2: reschedule a different job's start time via the board's
    # inline time input — the one control confirmed (during manual QA)
    # to actually push a schedule-change alert.
    owner_session
    |> set_field("[data-test='job-#{reschedule_job.id}-start-time-input']", "13:30:00")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(job_row(reschedule_job.id, "Unacknowledged"))
    |> assert_has(job_row(reschedule_job.id, "moved from"))

    # Step 3: the cleaner sees the loud alert on /field and
    # acknowledges it; the owner's board reflects the ack.
    cleaner_session = log_in(cleaner_session, cleaner, password)

    cleaner_session
    |> visit!("/field")
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='schedule-alert']"))
    |> click(css("[data-test$='-acknowledge-button']"))
    |> settle()

    owner_session
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> assert_has(job_row(reschedule_job.id, "Acknowledged"))

    # Step 4: cancel a job — it stays visible with a Cancelled badge
    # and Unacknowledged status.
    owner_session
    |> click(css("[data-test='job-#{cancel_job.id}'] button", text: "Cancel"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='job-#{cancel_job.id}-cancelled-badge']"))
    |> assert_has(job_row(cancel_job.id, "Unacknowledged"))

    # Step 5: backdate the cancellation alert past the escalation
    # window (10 minutes, per CleanerCrm.Notifications) — verify it
    # flips to Escalated/SMS on next read.
    cancel_notification =
      Notifications.list_notifications(scope)
      |> Enum.find(&(&1.job_id == cancel_job.id and &1.kind == :schedule_change))

    {:ok, _} =
      cancel_notification
      |> Ecto.Changeset.change(pushed_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -700, :second))
      |> CleanerCrm.Repo.update()

    owner_session
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> assert_has(job_row(cancel_job.id, "Escalated"))

    # Step 6: the audit trail reconstructs the reschedule and
    # cancellation, filtered by actor and record type. The actor
    # select's option value is the user's id, not their email (see
    # `actor_options/1` in audit_live.ex).
    owner_session
    |> visit!("/audit")
    |> set_field("#filter_actor", to_string(owner.id))
    |> set_field("#filter_subject_type", "Job")
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='audit-entries']", text: "rescheduled"))
    |> assert_has(css("[data-test='audit-entries']", text: "cancelled"))
  end

  defp job_row(job_id), do: css("[data-test='job-#{job_id}']")
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.PreferredCleanerContinuityTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 4 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): a recurring plan's
  visits default to its preferred cleaner, a one-off reassignment
  warns but doesn't rewrite the plan, and a no-preference plan warns
  on nothing.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling

  feature "recurring plans default to (and protect) the preferred cleaner", %{session: session} do
    %{owner_scope: scope, owner: owner, cleaner: preferred, password: password} =
      account_with_owner_and_cleaner()

    other_cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Journey4 QA Client"})
    property = client |> then(&property_fixture(scope, &1, %{service_address: "4 Plan Pl"}))

    session = log_in(session, owner, password)

    start_date = Date.utc_today() |> Date.add(7) |> Date.to_iso8601()

    session
    |> visit!("/schedule/plans/new")
    |> set_field("#plan_property_id", property.id)
    |> set_field("#plan_cleaner_id", to_string(preferred.id))
    |> set_field("#plan_recurrence", "weekly")
    |> set_field("#plan_start_date", start_date)
    |> set_field("#plan_occurrence_count", "3")
    |> click(css("[data-test='save-plan-button']"))
    |> settle()

    [plan] = Scheduling.list_recurring_plans_for_property(scope, property)
    visits = Scheduling.list_jobs(scope) |> Enum.filter(&(&1.recurring_plan_id == plan.id))
    assert length(visits) == 3
    assert Enum.all?(visits, &(&1.cleaner_id == preferred.id))

    [first_visit, second_visit, third_visit] = Enum.sort_by(visits, & &1.scheduled_date)

    session
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> set_field(
      "[data-test='job-#{first_visit.id}-cleaner-select']",
      to_string(other_cleaner.id)
    )
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "assigned away from the client's preferred cleaner"))

    reloaded_plan = Scheduling.get_recurring_plan!(scope, plan.id)
    assert reloaded_plan.cleaner_id == preferred.id

    for visit <- [second_visit, third_visit] do
      reloaded = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, visit.id)
      assert reloaded.cleaner_id == preferred.id
    end

    # Second plan, no preferred cleaner — reassigning a visit warns
    # about nothing.
    session
    |> visit!("/schedule/plans/new")
    |> set_field("#plan_property_id", property.id)
    |> set_field("#plan_recurrence", "weekly")
    |> set_field("#plan_start_date", Date.utc_today() |> Date.add(60) |> Date.to_iso8601())
    |> set_field("#plan_occurrence_count", "2")
    |> click(css("[data-test='save-plan-button']"))
    |> settle()

    [_first_plan, second_plan] = Scheduling.list_recurring_plans_for_property(scope, property)
    second_visit = Scheduling.list_jobs(scope) |> Enum.find(&(&1.recurring_plan_id == second_plan.id))
    refute second_visit.cleaner_id

    session
    |> visit!("/schedule")
    |> set_field(
      "[data-test='job-#{second_visit.id}-cleaner-select']",
      to_string(other_cleaner.id)
    )
    |> settle()
    |> refute_has(css("body", text: "assigned away from the client's preferred cleaner"))
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.Journeys.PayrollCloseTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Journey 5 (.code_my_spec/qa/journey_plan.md): a pay period with a
  mix of hourly and piece-rate jobs, a forgotten clock-out that blocks
  export until resolved, and a CSV export that matches the on-screen
  totals once it's unblocked.

  Nulling a clock-out is done directly through `Repo` — this test's
  equivalent of the sanctioned psql step from manual QA.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.FeatureCase, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking

  feature "a pay period closes correctly once every clock-out is resolved", %{session: session} do
    %{owner_scope: scope, owner: owner, cleaner: cleaner, password: password} =
      account_with_owner_and_cleaner()

    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Journey5 QA Client"})
    property = property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "5 Payroll Way"})

    today = Date.utc_today()

    hourly_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        pay_type: :hourly,
        hourly_rate_cents: 2500,
        agreed_price_cents: 8000,
        status: :completed
      })

    piece_rate_job =
      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: today,
        start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[15:00:00],
        pay_type: :piece_rate,
        piece_rate_cents: 4500,
        agreed_price_cents: 4500,
        status: :completed
      })

    {:ok, hourly_entry} =
      TimeTracking.create_time_entry(scope, %{
        job_id: hourly_job.id,
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        clocked_in_at: DateTime.new!(today, ~T[09:00:00]),
        clocked_out_at: DateTime.new!(today, ~T[11:00:00])
      })

    {:ok, _piece_entry} =
      TimeTracking.create_time_entry(scope, %{
        job_id: piece_rate_job.id,
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        clocked_in_at: DateTime.new!(today, ~T[13:00:00]),
        clocked_out_at: DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00])
      })

    session = log_in(session, owner, password)

    session
    |> visit!("/timesheets")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "$50.00"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "$45.00"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "$95.00"))

    # Introduce a forgotten clock-out — the entry gets flagged and
    # export is blocked.
    {:ok, _} =
      hourly_entry
      |> Ecto.Changeset.change(clocked_out_at: nil)
      |> CleanerCrm.Repo.update()

    session
    |> visit!("/timesheets")
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Missing clock-out"))
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "Resolve the unresolved time entry before exporting"))

    disabled? =
      Wallaby.Browser.execute_script(
        session,
        "return document.querySelector('[data-test=\"export-csv-button\"]').disabled",
        fn v -> send(self(), {:disabled, v}) end
      )

    assert_receive {:disabled, true}
    disabled?

    # Resolve it via the timesheet form — pay recomputes and export
    # unblocks.
    session
    |> set_field(
      "#resolve-form-#{hourly_job.id} input[name='time_entry[clock_out_time]']",
      "11:00:00"
    )
    |> click(css("#resolve-form-#{hourly_job.id} button"))
    |> settle()
    |> assert_has(css("body", text: "$95.00"))
    |> refute_has(css("body", text: "Missing clock-out"))

    export_enabled? =
      Wallaby.Browser.execute_script(
        session,
        "return !document.querySelector('[data-test=\"export-csv-button\"]').disabled",
        fn v -> send(self(), {:enabled, v}) end
      )

    assert_receive {:enabled, true}
    export_enabled?

    # Cross-check the export against the on-screen total.
    period = TimeTracking.current_pay_period(scope)
    {:ok, csv} = TimeTracking.export_pay_period_csv(scope, period)
    assert csv =~ owner.email == false
    assert csv =~ cleaner.email
    assert csv =~ "$95.00"

content.content:
1	# QA Journey Results — Cleaner CRM
2	
3	## Status
4	
5	Pass — all 5 journeys pass. Journey 1 initially failed its checklist-template step on a high-severity defect; that fix, plus two other defects found in Journeys 3 and 5, were deployed mid-run and all three are re-verified live.
6	
7	## Journey Results
8	
9	### Journey 1: New client to paid invoice
10	
11	**Pass** (after a mid-run fix — see below). Built one continuous fresh data thread — client "Journey1 QA Client" → property "742 Evergreen Terrace, Springfield" (full access details: lockbox 4517, alarm 9823, parking, pet notes, eco-friendly preference) → per-room quote ($210.00 = 3 bedrooms × $50 + 2 bathrooms × $30, correct math) → job for today, assigned to qa-cleaner, hourly pay ($25/hr) → cleaner clocked in/out and finished the job → invoice auto-generated with correct client name and $210.00 amount → "Charge card on file" → Charge Pending → simulated `POST /webhooks/stripe payment_intent.succeeded` → invoice flipped to **Paid**. `/audit` showed the price-bearing entries (quote sent, total cents 21000; job created; job completed).
12	
13	Initial run hit a blocker on "Create a room-by-room checklist template for that property at /quality/templates/new": the "Add Task" button never added a row to the template form, confirmed via direct page-level event dispatch that the server-side embed never grew from zero items. As a direct consequence the job's checklist had 0 items, so the cleaner had nothing to check off, and the paid invoice's "Proof of Work" section read "No completed checklist recorded" instead of showing checklist completion + photos. Filed as `79cdea90` (high) plus a compounding selector bug `a6b89e3c` (medium) found while diagnosing it.

## Wallaby Regression Tests (Phase 3)

All 5 journeys are codified as Wallaby feature tests under `test/journeys/`, each driving a real headless Chrome session against a real (test-env) Phoenix endpoint — not `Phoenix.ConnTest` simulation:

- `test/journeys/new_client_to_paid_invoice_test.exs` — Journey 1, two browser sessions (owner + cleaner), ends by hitting the real `/webhooks/stripe` endpoint with `Req` to flip the invoice to Paid.
- `test/journeys/cleaner_day_test.exs` — Journey 2, one session; a second cleaner's job exists only as a fixture (never logged in) to test the "not assigned to you" isolation.
- `test/journeys/schedule_chaos_test.exs` — Journey 3, two sessions (owner + cleaner); the escalation-window backdate is a direct `Repo` update (this test's equivalent of the sanctioned psql step).
- `test/journeys/preferred_cleaner_continuity_test.exs` — Journey 4, one session, two recurring plans.
- `test/journeys/payroll_close_test.exs` — Journey 5, one session; the forgotten-clock-out is a direct `Repo` update, same rationale as Journey 3.

Setup added to make this possible (none of it existed before this session): the `wallaby` dependency (`mix.exs`); `config/test.exs` (`sql_sandbox: true`, `server: true`, `:wallaby` driver config); a guarded `Phoenix.Ecto.SQL.Sandbox` plug in `lib/cleaner_crm_web/endpoint.ex` (only compiled in when `sql_sandbox` is set, so dev/prod are untouched); `test/support/feature_case.ex`; `test/support/fixtures/journey_fixtures.ex` (shared owner+cleaner account setup, `log_in/3`, and three helpers — `set_field/3`, `check_field/2`, `settle/2` — needed because this app's `<label for=id>` markup isn't one Wallaby's label-lookup resolves, native date/time inputs don't accept `send_keys` reliably, and `assert_has`'s default 3s retry doesn't reliably cover either a fresh LiveView mount's autofocus race or the beat after a save/redirect in this environment); a tiny fixture PNG for photo-upload tests.

Two things worth flagging about the test run itself:
- The photo-upload steps in Journeys 1 and 2 exercise `attach_file` but don't wait for the upload to visibly complete — LiveView's upload channel never finished within any wait tried (up to 10s) in this headless-Chrome + Wallaby combination, most likely an environment compatibility gap rather than an app bug (real photo upload was independently confirmed working via interactive QA in this same session).
- Writing Journey 2 surfaced the `ec8e6c8d` invoice-crash bug listed above — a job fixture without `agreed_price_cents` (matching what `Recurrence.job_attrs/1` actually produces) crashed the LiveView on `mark_complete` until the test's fixture was corrected to always set a price, same as the real job-creation form does.

Final state: `PORT=4002 MIX_ENV=test mix test test/journeys/` → 5 features, 0 failures, run 3+ times each for stability. `PORT=4002 MIX_ENV=test mix test` (full suite) → 5 features, 163 tests, 0 failures — no regressions from the Wallaby setup changes. `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors` and `mix format --check-formatted` both clean. The dev release was never touched by any of this (`server: true`/`sql_sandbox: true` are test-env-only config).
